lanes.headline: superbot-next's whole "degrade instead of refuse to boot" decision rests on a premise its own composition root falsifies: sb/spec/config.py:252-255 justifies DEGRADE because "refuse-to-boot ... darked the WHOLE bot when every slash command still serves", but main.py:616 hardcodes `sync_remote(bot, committed, enabled=False)` and the only other sync leg is gated on SB_DATA_PLANE=test — so this root never registers ANY of its 27 slash paths with Discord. Without message_content, all 422 compiled commands are unreachable, not 1,300 of 1,327 with 27 surviving; the bot reports /ready 200; the one notice it records lands in a 256-entry in-process ring with zero sinks, is suppressed on every subsequent boot by a durable latch, and the in-Discord card that would show it (`!platform findings`) is a frozen literal that always reads "*(none)*". The successor's bootstrap contract must make "online" mean "a named, counted, reachable command surface", and must put every degraded state on a sink that survives the process.

strengths.claim: The load-first ordering of the central access gate is not convention — it is a 4-assertion invariant test that runs in CI (code-quality.yml:279 `pytest tests/ -v -n auto`) over the REAL 59-entry config.INITIAL_EXTENSIONS list (AST-counted at this pin: 59 entries, index 0 == cogs.bootstrap_access_cog, exactly 1 occurrence, cogs.admin_cog at index 1). Unlike superbot-next's navigation_golden guard, this one CANNOT be green over an empty population: `INITIAL_EXTENSIONS[0]` raises IndexError on an empty list.
strengths.contradicts: The task prompt frames this as 'loads FIRST by explicit INITIAL_EXTENSIONS ordering' — i.e. as an ordering convention. It is stronger than that: it is CI-enforced with an index assertion that cannot pass vacuously. superbot-next has no equivalent guard because it has no extension list to order.
strengths.prevents_failure: A cog registering commands before the central command-access resolver is installed — commands admitted, or blocked by the legacy guard, with no policy applied (the 'stranded operator in a fresh guild' case named in the test docstring).
strengths.guard_population: The real config.INITIAL_EXTENSIONS list — 59 string entries at this pin, AST-counted, exit 0. It is the same object bot1.py:722 iterates and parity/harness/boot.py:203 replays, not a model of it. It cannot be empty: index [0] would raise.
strengths.simpler_than_counterpart: superbot-next replaces the ordering problem with a compile-time manifest, which removes this failure class but also removes runtime cog load/unload entirely (see R4-D10).
strengths.successor_recommendation: Keep an ordering guard shaped like this one — an index assertion over the live registration list, run in CI. Its value is that it is structurally impossible to satisfy over an empty set.

strengths.claim: Extension load failure is recorded rather than swallowed, and it changes live governance state: each failure is written to startup_outcome, alerted on the ops webhook, and any subsystem whose entry-point commands are now absent is demoted to INTERNAL so it stops being advertised. startup_outcome has 3 distinct readers outside bot1.py (health_snapshot_service.py:440, platform_consistency.py:1171, webhook_reporter.py:174).
strengths.quote:
for ext in config.INITIAL_EXTENSIONS:
        try:
            await bot.load_extension(ext)
            startup_outcome.record_extension_success(ext)
            logger.info("✅ Loaded %s", ext)
        except Exception as exc:
            startup_outcome.record_extension_failure(ext, exc)
            failed_exts.add(ext)
            logger.error(
                "❌ Failed to load %s: %s: %s",
                ext,
                type(exc).__name__,
                exc,
                exc_info=True,
            )
            if reporter:
                await reporter.on_cog_fail(ext, exc)
strengths.prevents_failure: A cog that failed to load leaving its subsystem still advertised as available in help/hub while every one of its commands is missing — the user-facing 'command exists in help, does nothing' failure.
strengths.guard_population: Every entry in INITIAL_EXTENSIONS (59 at this pin) on every real boot; the demotion pass runs only when failed_exts is non-empty, and it walks the SUBSYSTEMS registry comparing declared entry_points against `{cmd.name for cmd in bot.commands}` on the live bot.
strengths.successor_recommendation: Preserve the three-part shape: record the failure as data, alert out-of-band, AND mutate the advertised surface so the failed subsystem stops appearing. The third part is the one most successors drop.

strengths.claim: The deterministic startup-outcome summary is posted to the ops webhook BEFORE bot.start(), explicitly so operators see boot health without waiting for on_ready — which means a boot that dies before READY still produces an out-of-band artifact. superbot-next has no equivalent: its _fail_startup (main.py:205-211) sets a phase and logs, and the composition root installs no alert sink at all (0 consumers of sb/kernel/observability/alerts.py outside tests).
strengths.contradicts: This same pre-connect timing is what makes R4-D05 dangerous: on a PrivilegedIntentsRequired crash loop the summary fires on every iteration reporting a healthy boot, because every cog loaded fine and the gateway failure happens after this line. The mechanism is right and the payload is wrong — do not smooth this into an unqualified strength.
strengths.prevents_failure: A boot that dies before READY leaving zero operator-visible trace outside container stdout.
strengths.new_failure_class: A pre-connect summary that reports OK for a boot that never connects — see R4-D05.
strengths.successor_recommendation: Keep the pre-connect out-of-band summary, but make it a two-phase contract: a 'boot reached pre-connect, N/M extensions loaded' notice AND a mandatory post-READY confirmation, so absence of the second is itself the alarm.

strengths.claim: A health-server bind failure is treated as a boot abort, not a warning: critical log + a dedicated webhook (on_health_startup_failed) + SystemExit(1). The comment at bot1.py:1016-1020 states the reasoning — 5s is generous because bind is a local syscall — and the sibling branch degrades honestly (a bind that neither fails nor signals within 5s logs a warning and continues).
strengths.prevents_failure: Running with a wedged orchestration probe: the replica never answers /ready, the platform cannot tell it is half-dead, and no restart is triggered.
strengths.simpler_than_counterpart: superbot-next has the same structural check (main.py:289-297) with a 10s timeout, but its failure path is _fail_startup — log only, no out-of-band notice.
strengths.successor_recommendation: Preserve: a probe that cannot bind is a boot abort, and the abort must reach a human channel, not just the log.

strengths.claim: `!platform lifecycle` reads a LIVE provider snapshot and degrades honestly when the provider is absent ('Provider not registered.'), so the operator-facing phase/accepting-commands line is a fact about this process. This is the direct counterpart of superbot-next's frozen literal (see R4-D03) and is why the owner's 2026-09-01 remark that the OLD bot is the docs/quality baseline extends to its operator surfaces.
strengths.contradicts: superbot-next/sb/domain/diagnostic/platform_views.py:274-286, where the same card is a hardcoded string that always reads 'Phase: **STARTING** · Accepting commands: **True** · Startup observed: **no**'.
strengths.prevents_failure: An operator reading a fabricated phase during a live incident and concluding the platform is fine.
strengths.successor_recommendation: Make it a hard rule for the successor: an operator diagnostic card either reads live state or says it cannot. A pinned literal in a diagnostic surface is a correctness bug, not a porting shortcut.

strengths.claim: Two independent in-Discord recovery levers exist for a failed/misbehaving cog, and the protection asymmetry is deliberate and documented: the panel Unload button refuses _PROTECTED_COGS while the prefix `!cog` command intentionally retains no protection because it is the operator's escape hatch when the panel will not open.
strengths.quote:
@commands.command(name="cog")
    @commands.is_owner()
    async def manage_cog(self, ctx, action: str, cog_name: str):
        """Load, unload, or reload a cog by name (underscores and _cog suffix optional).

        The prefix command intentionally retains no critical-cog
        protection — it is the operator's escape hatch when the panel
        won't open or a protected cog needs to be unloaded. The panel
        Unload button refuses protected cogs (see ``_PROTECTED_COGS``).
        """
strengths.prevents_failure: A single broken cog forcing a redeploy: the owner can reload or unload it in-channel and keep the rest of the bot serving.
strengths.simpler_than_counterpart: superbot-next has no equivalent whatsoever — 0 occurrences of reload_extension under sb/ (see R4-D10).
strengths.successor_recommendation: This is the concrete form of the owner's COG-PORTABLE requirement (2026-08-23). A successor that compiles its surface at boot must still expose a runtime load/unload/reload lever with two access paths, one of which does not depend on a panel rendering.

strengths.claim: Intents are computed from typed config approvals rather than hardcoded, so the whole PrivilegedIntentsRequired failure class is designed out at the source: the client only ever requests a privileged intent whose approval env asserts Discord-side approval. This is the single clearest structural improvement over superbot in this lane.
strengths.quote:
def build_intents(cfg: object):
    """Intents.default() + the two privileged intents iff approved."""
    if not DISCORD_AVAILABLE:
        raise RuntimeError("discord is not installed — no gateway in this container")
    intents = discord.Intents.default()
    intents.message_content = bool(getattr(cfg, "SB_INTENT_MSGCONTENT_OK", False))
    intents.members = bool(getattr(cfg, "SB_INTENT_MEMBERS_OK", False))
    return intents
strengths.contradicts: superbot/disbot/bot1.py:76-78 sets `intents.message_content = True` and `intents.members = True` unconditionally, with no approval gate anywhere in the repo — see R4-D05.
strengths.prevents_failure: PrivilegedIntentsRequired crash-loop: the bot never comes online at all because an unapproved privileged intent was requested unconditionally.
strengths.simpler_than_counterpart: Two lines of getattr replace a whole class of deploy-time outage.
strengths.new_failure_class: It converts a loud total failure into a quiet partial one — which is only an improvement if the degrade is actually announced and the remaining surface actually serves. At this pin neither holds (R4-D01, R4-D02).
strengths.successor_recommendation: Preserve the approval-gated intent computation verbatim. Pair it with a boot-time assertion that the surviving reachable command count is > 0, or it buys nothing.

strengths.area: degraded state: DB down / still starting
strengths.claim: Readiness is a decision table with a named reason per row and it is DB-aware: RUNNING + DB down returns 503 db_unavailable, and STARTING returns 503 still_starting rather than the shipped bot's 200. superbot's /ready (healthserver.py:114-137) checks only bot.is_ready() and the lifecycle phase — it will answer 200 with a dead pool.
strengths.contradicts: superbot/disbot/healthserver.py:114-137, whose /ready is gateway+phase only and is NOT DB-aware — the older bot is the better documented one but the newer one is right here.
strengths.prevents_failure: An orchestrator routing production traffic to, or declaring healthy, a replica whose DB pool is down or which is still applying migrations.
strengths.simpler_than_counterpart: One pure function with an explicit truth table in its docstring, versus superbot's inline boolean pair.
strengths.new_failure_class: The table has no degrade dimension: it cannot express 'online but the command surface is dead' (R4-D09).
strengths.successor_recommendation: Preserve the table shape and the named reasons; ADD a row for capability degrade so 'ready' means 'a counted command surface is reachable', not merely 'gateway up and DB up'.

strengths.claim: Boot-gate leg A is a hard pre-connect refusal — the committed manifest snapshot is recompiled in-process (P1..P9) and any divergence returns FAILED_STARTUP before the gateway, the health server, or the DB pool matter. Its population is the real committed artifact and is large and non-empty at this pin (422 command / 640 custom_id / 314 panel / 23 event / 102 setting_key nodes, counted from manifest.snapshot.json, exit 0). It has two independent callers: the live root and the verify-boot profile.
strengths.contradicts: The sibling finding that superbot-next's tests/unit/navigation_golden guard runs green over a registry its own conftest clears. Leg A is the counter-example inside the SAME repo: same team, same era, but a real non-empty committed artifact and a hard fail. The repo's problem is not that it cannot build real guards — it is that it also ships fake ones and does not distinguish them.
strengths.prevents_failure: A deploy whose committed snapshot disagrees with what the compiler produces booting anyway and serving a command surface nobody compiled — manifest drift reaching production half-applied.
strengths.guard_population: The committed manifest.snapshot.json, recompiled in-process. 422 command / 640 custom_id / 314 panel / 23 event / 102 setting_key / 49 subsystem_key / 74 table nodes at this pin (counted). Not a model of the artifact — it IS the artifact, compared by stable_hash. It could only be empty if the committed snapshot file were empty, which would itself be a divergence.
strengths.simpler_than_counterpart: superbot has no equivalent single pre-connect structural gate; its integrity checks are spread across scripts/ and CI.
strengths.successor_recommendation: Preserve as the model for every guard in the successor: name the population, make it the committed artifact rather than a rebuilt model of it, and make divergence a refusal before anything connects.

strengths.claim: A side-effect-free full boot profile exists (SB_VERIFY_BOOT) that is structurally incapable of touching the world — no gateway is constructed, no token is used, the poll supervisor and outbox relay are simply never built, and preflight REFUSES the mode on a non-test data plane — and a weekly workflow runs it against a restored backup. This is the only mechanism in either repo that proves a backup is restorable-AND-bootable rather than merely restorable.
strengths.quote:
Side-effect-free BY CONSTRUCTION:
  (a) no gateway connect and no bot token — `assert_intents` approval is
      irrelevant (nothing connects); outbound sends are impossible (no
      transport is built).
  (b) boot-reconcile + outbox relay SUPPRESSED — this module simply never
      builds the PollSupervisor / relay lanes; reaching readiness is a
      preflight → boot-gate → db.init fact, and boot-reconcile is a
      POST-ready steady-state step (vocab ⑤.3), so suppressing it does not
      weaken the boots-to-ready proof.
  (c) plane-fenced — preflight REFUSES SB_VERIFY_BOOT on a non-test plane
      (sb/kernel/config/preflight; the rails compose).
strengths.contradicts: Its own CI leg cannot currently fail: .github/workflows/restore-verify.yml:124 pipes it into `tee` with no pipefail (R4-D04). The profile is a real strength; the proof it feeds is currently green over every failure. Do not record this row as a working guard.
strengths.prevents_failure: A backup that restores but does not boot — discovered only during a real outage, at the moment it cannot be fixed.
strengths.guard_population: The restored production backup in the workflow's service container, exercised through preflight -> boot-gate leg A -> db.init (real pool, real migration runner, real verify_applied_checksums) -> lifecycle STARTING/RUNNING -> the dry-run invariant sweep. The population is a real restored database, not a fixture. It is NOT currently load-bearing because the exit code is swallowed by the pipe.
strengths.simpler_than_counterpart: superbot has backup-db.yml but no boot-the-restore leg at all.
strengths.successor_recommendation: Adopt the profile as designed AND fix the pipe. A restorability proof whose exit code is discarded is worse than none, because it produces a weekly green signal.

strengths.claim: Which capabilities die with which intent is DATA, declared next to the intent, not an ad-hoc branch: INTENT_CONTRACT names message_content -> ('prefix','fuzzy','triggers','nl_message','passive_onmessage') and members -> ('member_join','member_leave','member_cache'), and intent_degradations() derives the boot's markers from that tuple. superbot has no such declaration anywhere — its two privileged intents are two bare assignments.
strengths.quote:
IntentSpec("message_content", privileged=True, required=False,
               approval_env="SB_INTENT_MSGCONTENT_OK",
               posture=IntentPosture.DEGRADE,
               degrades=("prefix", "fuzzy", "triggers", "nl_message",
                         "passive_onmessage")),
    IntentSpec("members", privileged=True, required=False,
               approval_env="SB_INTENT_MEMBERS_OK",
               posture=IntentPosture.DEGRADE,
               degrades=("member_join", "member_leave", "member_cache")),
strengths.contradicts: The declaration is richer than the consumption: main.py:664-667 consults exactly ONE of the five declared message_content classes ('prefix'). The other four ('fuzzy','triggers','nl_message','passive_onmessage') are declared and never read by the composition root at this pin.
strengths.prevents_failure: An intent denial silently disabling capabilities nobody enumerated — the blast radius is written down next to the cause instead of being rediscovered from symptoms.
strengths.guard_population: tests/unit/platform_governance/test_s15_governance.py:26-32 iterates the REAL INTENT_CONTRACT tuple (2 entries at this pin, both asserted privileged/required=False/DEGRADE/non-empty degrades). Honest caveat: it is a `for` loop over a tuple, so it would pass VACUOUSLY if INTENT_CONTRACT were ever emptied — no length assertion pins the population.
strengths.successor_recommendation: Preserve the declaration. Add the length assertion the current test lacks, and make the composition root consume every declared class rather than one of five — an unread degrade class is a silent capability loss with a written-down name nobody checks.

defects.claim: The stated justification for choosing DEGRADE over refuse-to-boot is false at this pin. sb/spec/config.py:252-255 says refuse-to-boot 'darked the WHOLE bot when every slash command still serves' — but main.py:616 hardcodes leg C to compare-only (`enabled=False`) and the only other sync leg (main.py:636) is gated by guild_sync_target(), which returns None unless SB_DATA_PLANE == 'test' AND SB_APPCMD_SYNC_GUILD_ID is set. On the prod plane this root registers ZERO of its own 27 slash paths with Discord. With message_content denied, all 422 compiled commands (395 prefix + 27 slash, counted from manifest.snapshot.json) are unreachable — not 1,300 of 1,327 with 27 surviving.
defects.quote:
# 13. boot-gate leg C — GLOBAL sync stays compare-only in the
        #     test-mode root (module docstring): the remote GLOBAL set is
        #     the OLD bot's until CUT-3; drift is logged, never fatal.
        from sb.app.tree_sync import sync_remote

        outcome = await sync_remote(bot, committed, enabled=False)
defects.contradicts: BOTH the prior audit's framing (1,300 of 1,327 dispatch targets unreachable, implying 27 survived) AND sb/spec/config.py:252-255's own written rationale for the DEGRADE posture. The design decision and the composition root disagree, 360 lines apart in the same repo.
defects.failure_scenario: The owner deploys superbot-next to the prod plane with the Discord portal's Message Content toggle off. Preflight passes (the intent is DEGRADE, not REQUIRED), the gateway connects, lifecycle goes RUNNING, /ready returns 200 'ready'. A user types `!help` — nothing happens, because the message feed was never armed (main.py:665-667). The same user opens the slash-command picker — superbot-next's 27 commands are not there, because leg C is compare-only and guild sync refuses the prod plane. Every one of the 422 compiled commands is unreachable. The only trace is `logger.info("message feed NOT armed: prefix class degraded (message_content unapproved)")` inside a boot INFO stream, and the health probe reports the release healthy.
defects.successor_recommendation: The successor's boot must compute and assert a REACHABLE command count after every gate — sum of (surfaces actually armed) x (commands registered on that surface) — and treat zero, or a drop past a declared floor, as FAILED_STARTUP. 'Degrade instead of refuse' is only safe when the surviving surface is proven to exist at boot, not assumed.

defects.claim: The degrade notice has no sink. emit_degrade_notices calls record_operator_finding, which appends to a module-level `deque(maxlen=256)` and emits one log line. sb/kernel/observability/alerts.py declares OperatorAlertSink / LoggingAlertSink / NullAlertSink / prepare_alert — and has ZERO consumers outside tests/ (counted). sb/app/main.py installs no alert sink at all (0 matches for 'AlertSink' or 'alerts.' in sb/app/*.py). No webhook adapter exists in sb/ (the only 'webhook' hits under sb/ are spec/manifest declarations).
defects.quote:
_findings: deque[OperatorFinding] = deque(maxlen=_BUFFER_SIZE)


def record_operator_finding(
    *,
    source: str,
    severity: str,
    summary: str,
    detail: str,
    correlation_id: object | None = None,
) -> OperatorFinding:
    """Record one persistent operator finding (the spec 08 §4 seam)."""
defects.contradicts: sb/kernel/observability/alerts.py:4-8 states the shipped WebhookReporter 'lands as a K5/observability SINK SPEC'. The spec landed; the adapter did not. Also contradicts the docstring's own word 'persistent' — the store is an in-process ring wiped by every restart.
defects.failure_scenario: Discord revokes message_content (verification lapse, or the owner toggles it while doing something else). On the next deploy emit_degrade_notices records a warning finding: 'privileged-intent degrade active: message_content'. It goes into a 256-entry in-process deque and one stdout line in a Railway log nobody is reading. No webhook fires, no Discord message is posted, no alert reaches the owner's phone. The process restarts an hour later and the ring is empty. The first human signal is a guild member reporting that commands stopped working.
defects.successor_recommendation: Make the sink a boot-time requirement, not an installable option: the successor should refuse to reach RUNNING unless at least one operator-alert sink that leaves the process (webhook, DM, log-drain) is installed and has been proven writable by a boot canary.

defects.claim: The operator diagnostic cards are frozen capture-world literals of the OLD bot, not live introspection. platform_views.py holds 21 hardcoded `_View(` entries (counted). `!platform lifecycle` ALWAYS renders 'Phase: **STARTING** · Accepting commands: **True** · Startup observed: **no**'; `!platform findings` ALWAYS renders 'open 0 · resolved 0 · ignored 0 · 0 total' with '*(none)*'. build_view_embed (platform_views.py:419-443) substitutes only four world tokens — channel id, guild id, timestamp, member tier — and never consults runtime state. The one LIVE consistency path (sb/domain/platform/consistency.py:collect_report) has exactly one caller, sb/domain/platform/ai_tasks.py:55, i.e. it is reachable only through the AI lane, not from the `!platform` cards.
defects.quote:
"lifecycle": _View(
        title='🔄 Lifecycle',
        description='Phase: **STARTING** · Accepting commands: **True** · Startup observed: **no**',
        fields=(
            ('Pending request',
             '_none_',
             False),
            ('Recent events',
             '_none recorded_',
             False),
        ),
        style_token="gold",
    ),
defects.contradicts: superbot/disbot/services/diagnostic_embeds.py:1252-1283, which reads a live provider snapshot and falls back to an honest 'Provider not registered.'. It also compounds R4-D02: the finding recorded by emit_degrade_notices is invisible on the exact card whose title is 'Health findings — open'.
defects.failure_scenario: superbot-next is degraded (message_content denied, or DRAINING, or a subsystem down). The owner opens Discord and runs `!platform lifecycle` to diagnose. The card reports phase STARTING and 'Accepting commands: True' — a string literal captured from the old bot. He runs `!platform findings`: '0 total', '*(none)*', green — while a warning finding sits in the ring. He concludes the platform is healthy and looks for the fault somewhere else. Worse: both cards are PREFIX commands, so under the very degrade he is diagnosing they do not dispatch at all.
defects.successor_recommendation: Ban pinned literals from any surface whose job is to report state. Where a port cannot yet introspect, the card must say so explicitly (superbot's 'Provider not registered.' shape). Add a source-level check that no module under a diagnostic/ path exports embed text containing a state word ('Phase:', 'open N', 'ready') as a literal.

defects.claim: The weekly restorability proof cannot fail. restore-verify.yml:124 runs `python3 -m sb.app.verify_boot | tee verify-report.json` with no `shell:` key and no `defaults:` key anywhere in the file (0 occurrences of 'pipefail' or 'shell:' across all 8 of superbot-next's workflow files, counted) — so GitHub Actions runs it under the implicit `bash -e {0}` default, without pipefail, and the step's exit status is tee's. verify_boot's own `main()` is careful to `return 0 if report.get("verified") else 1`; that exit code is discarded. Measured locally on the same pipe shape: `bash -e` -> exit 0; `bash -eo pipefail` -> exit 1. The restore step at line 112 (`zcat "$DUMP" | psql ...`) is the same class.
defects.quote:
- name: Verify-boot + dry-run sweep (SB_VERIFY_BOOT, test-plane forced)
        env:
          SB_VERIFY_BOOT: "true"
          SB_DATA_PLANE: "test"
          SB_TEST_DB_HOSTS: "localhost"
          DATABASE_URL: "postgresql://verify:verify@localhost:5432/restore_target"
          DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN_PRODUCTION: "verify-boot-placeholder"  # never used: no gateway is built
        run: python3 -m sb.app.verify_boot | tee verify-report.json

      - name: Open issue on failure
        if: failure()
defects.contradicts: superbot's own workflows DO guard this: `set -euo pipefail` at .github/workflows/code-quality.yml:51 (plus three more workflows with `set -uo pipefail`). superbot-next has zero. It also contradicts the workflow's own failure copy at line 137-138: 'the backup layer is NOT proven restorable right now (do not cut over on a red proof)' — the job it belongs to cannot go red for this reason.
defects.failure_scenario: A week's backup restores into a schema the current migration ladder cannot apply (checksum drift, a migration added out of order). `python3 -m sb.app.verify_boot` prints {"verified": false, "stage": "db_init", ...} and returns 1. `tee` returns 0, so the step passes; `if: failure()` never fires; no issue is opened. The dashboard shows a green weekly restore-verify. Months later the owner needs the backup during a real incident, restores it, and the bot will not boot — with a green proof history saying it would.
defects.successor_recommendation: Every CI step that pipes must declare `shell: bash` (which supplies -eo pipefail) or `set -euo pipefail` inline. Better: have the verifier write its own machine-readable verdict file and add an explicit assertion step that reads it, so the proof does not depend on shell exit-code plumbing at all.

defects.claim: bot1.py:76-78 requests both privileged intents unconditionally, with no approval gate anywhere in the repo. PrivilegedIntentsRequired is raised by discord.py inside `bot.start(config.DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN)` (bot1.py:1327). Nothing catches it: `_maybe_backoff_on_rate_limit` handles ONLY `discord.HTTPException` with status 429, so it returns False and there is no backoff; the module-level `except Exception` logs one line and the process exits 1. Because the startup-outcome webhook is posted BEFORE bot.start (bot1.py:1309-1318), every iteration of the resulting restart loop emits a fresh operator webhook reporting boot health as OK — all 59 extensions loaded fine.
defects.contradicts: The task prompt's framing that 'superbot's bootstrap_access_cog loads FIRST ... and keeps an operator escape hatch'. Under an intent denial superbot has no degraded mode and no escape hatch at all — it never reaches on_ready, so no cog, no panel and no prefix command exists to escape into. It also inverts R4-S03: superbot's best boot-notification mechanism actively reports success during this outage.
defects.failure_scenario: Discord turns off Message Content Intent (verification lapse at the 100-guild threshold, or a portal change). superbot requests message_content + members unconditionally, discord.py raises PrivilegedIntentsRequired during login, nothing catches it, `_maybe_backoff_on_rate_limit` declines to back off because it is not an HTTPException 429, the process exits 1 and Railway restarts it immediately in a tight loop. On every iteration the owner receives another startup-summary webhook embed reporting the boot as OK. The bot is never online, the alerts say it booted fine, and the only honest signal is a stderr traceback in the container log.
defects.successor_recommendation: Take superbot-next's approval-gated intents (R4-S07) AND add what neither repo has: a typed classification of terminal login failures (PrivilegedIntentsRequired / LoginFailure / 429) each with its own backoff and its own out-of-band message. A restart loop that emits a success notice per iteration is worse than silence.

defects.area: degraded state: DB down at boot
defects.claim: `await db.init()` runs at bot1.py:963 — before `reporter.start()` (bot1.py:~985) and before the health server is spawned (bot1.py:1011) — and is not wrapped in a try. A DB failure therefore propagates before any notification channel exists, before any lifecycle phase is recorded, and before /ready can answer anything but connection-refused.
defects.quote:
await db.init()

    # Acquire the runtime instance lock now that migrations (including
    # 034_bot_runtime_lock) have run. If another replica holds the lock
    # this raises ``SystemExit(0)`` — Railway treats that as a graceful
    # exit and does not crash-loop the loser. ``_runtime`` and
defects.contradicts: Contrasts with the same file's careful treatment of the health-bind failure (R4-S04), which DOES webhook before exiting. The repo knows how to do this; the DB path predates it.
defects.failure_scenario: Postgres is unreachable at deploy (credential rotation, provider incident, a migration lock held by a stuck replica). `await db.init()` raises before the WebhookReporter's aiohttp session is started, so no webhook can be sent; no lifecycle phase is set, so the /lifecycle endpoint has nothing to show; the health server has not been spawned, so /ready is connection-refused rather than a 503 with a reason. The module-level handler logs 'Critical startup error' once and exits 1; the platform crash-loops. The owner sees only 'bot offline' and must open container logs to learn it is the database.
defects.successor_recommendation: Order the boot so the two observability channels — a bound health endpoint that can answer 503 with a reason, and an out-of-band alert sink — are the FIRST things established, before the DB, the gateway, or any manifest work. Every later failure then has somewhere to be reported.

defects.claim: The command-access denial feedback path swallows a Forbidden into a DEBUG log, which is below the default INFO level, so a permission-degraded denial is invisible to both the user and anyone reading logs at default verbosity. This is the same shape in both surfaces (prefix at :156-167, slash at :204-229). superbot handles discord.Forbidden in 83 places across 43 files under disbot/ (counted) — this lane did not classify how many of those 83 produce user-visible feedback rather than a log line.
defects.contradicts: The module docstring at bootstrap_access_cog.py:22-27 promises 'Denial feedback is surface-appropriate' and the inline comment at :150-155 says the send exists so the operator does not see 'the same "invoked but not completed" silent failure that PR-4 was written to eliminate'. When the bot lacks Send Messages, that exact silent failure returns, and the fallback is DEBUG.
defects.failure_scenario: A guild admin removes the bot's Send Messages permission in a channel where prefix commands are also channel-restricted (the `selected_channels` mode this guard exists for). A member runs a command: resolve_command_access denies it, `ctx.send(decision.feedback, delete_after=10)` raises Forbidden, the except swallows it into logger.debug — below default INFO — and the member sees absolutely nothing at all. The INFO deny line that follows names the reason but never leaves the process. The member concludes the bot is broken; the operator has no in-Discord way to learn the bot cannot speak in that channel.
defects.successor_recommendation: When the primary feedback channel is Forbidden, escalate rather than downgrade: fall back to an ephemeral interaction reply where one is possible, and record an operator finding at WARNING naming the guild and channel, so 'the bot cannot speak here' becomes a diagnosable state instead of a debug line.

defects.claim: The consistency collector's FATAL promotion is dead code. _collect_findings tests `getattr(f, "severity", "") == "fatal"`, but findings.py:32 defines SEVERITIES = ("info", "warning", "error", "critical") and record_operator_finding coerces any severity outside that tuple to "error" (findings.py:58-59). No code path can produce a finding whose severity is "fatal", so the readiness report can classify the findings section as WARNING or CLEAN but never FATAL.
defects.contradicts: The module's own severity vocabulary. Two files in the same kernel disagree on the name of the top severity, and the disagreement is silent because `getattr(..., "")` cannot raise.
defects.failure_scenario: A CRITICAL operator finding is recorded — the spec 08 §4 outbox DEAD path, or an ErrorPolicy.ESCALATE_FINDING route. The owner asks the AI operator lane for a platform consistency report (the one live caller, ai_tasks.py:55). The findings section comes back as WARNING '1 operator finding(s)' with no severity breakdown, indistinguishable from a benign info finding. The readiness card renders amber rather than red and the critical escalation is triaged as noise.
defects.successor_recommendation: Severity must be a shared enum imported by both producer and consumer, never a string compared by literal. A successor should make any status-mapping table exhaustive over that enum and fail to import if a name is unhandled.

defects.claim: The degrade is evaluated AFTER the bot is online and after readiness flips green: main.py sets STARTING and connects the gateway at :600-606, sets RUNNING at :609, and only then reads the intent markers at :654 and decides not to arm the message feed at :665-667. readiness_decision (health.py:75-96) has no degrade dimension at all — gateway up + RUNNING + DB up is unconditionally 200 'ready'. There is no state the health payload can express between 'ready' and 'not_ready'.
defects.quote:
# 14b. the message feed — prefix-command dispatch + the passive XP
        #      chat award (band 4, D-0061; report §4.2's other feeds stay
        #      dormant successors). Registered AFTER the markers per spec
        #      14 §2.B: a degraded ``prefix`` class means no registration.

defects.failure_scenario: A release goes out with message_content unapproved. main.py:609 sets RUNNING, /ready starts answering 200 'ready', and the deploy pipeline marks the release healthy and stops watching. Steps 14 and 14b then decide not to arm the message feed. The uptime monitor, the platform health check and the deploy dashboard all stay green forever while 395 prefix commands are dead. Nothing in the readiness payload can express 'online, zero commands reachable'.
defects.successor_recommendation: Compute the capability set BEFORE flipping RUNNING, and make the readiness payload carry it: `{"status":"ready","degraded":["prefix"],"reachable_commands":27}`. A successor should treat reachable_commands == 0 as not_ready, not as ready-with-a-log-line.

defects.claim: There is no in-Discord recovery lever for anything below process level: 0 occurrences of `reload_extension` anywhere under sb/ (counted), no cog model, and the only runtime lever is `restart` (sb/domain/admin/handlers.py:101), i.e. a process exit. sb/domain/setup/recovery.py is a setup-wizard section retry surface, not a platform recovery surface. Every degraded state enumerated in this lane — missing intent, failed manifest gate, DB down, missing config — is recoverable only by changing an environment variable or pushing code and redeploying.
defects.contradicts: The owner's standing requirement (2026-08-23): 'I should be able to add exiting cogs to it on demand, or be able to slightly alter an existing cog so that it works with this bot.' A boot-time manifest compiler with a hard parity gate and no runtime load path cannot add a cog on demand — the compile-and-refuse design and the cog-portability requirement pull in opposite directions, and this lane found nothing in the repo that reconciles them.
defects.failure_scenario: One subsystem's manifest is wrong after a merge. Boot-gate leg A refuses the whole process (FAILED_STARTUP, exit 1) rather than degrading that one subsystem, and the platform crash-loops with the entire bot down. In superbot the equivalent is one failed extension: the bot boots, the subsystem is demoted to INTERNAL, and the owner types `!cog reload economy` in a channel to fix it. In superbot-next the owner must revert or fix the manifest and redeploy, with the bot fully offline in between.
defects.successor_recommendation: The owner has to decide the trade explicitly and it should be written down: all-or-nothing compile-time parity buys the no-architectural-debt property he asked for, but it costs the on-demand cog portability he also asked for. A middle contract is possible — per-subsystem gating, where a subsystem that fails its own leg is quarantined and the rest boots — and that is the version that satisfies both statements.

defects.claim: The once-per-state-change latch is durable (install_platform_state_store is wired at main.py:324, before the notice at :658) but the finding STORE it writes into is not (an in-process deque, R4-D02). The two combine so that a persistent degrade is announced exactly once, into a buffer the next restart wipes, and never again — because the persisted latch then suppresses every subsequent emission.
defects.quote:
current = _render_state(markers)
    persisted = _READ(DEGRADE_STATE_KEY)
    if persisted == current:
        return False
defects.contradicts: The module docstring at platform_governance.py:11-13 presents the latch as a virtue ('a redeploy under the SAME denial does not re-fire (merge=deploy = minutes apart, Q-0193)'). Paired with a non-durable finding store it is the opposite: it converts a permanent degraded state into a one-time event that leaves no record.
defects.failure_scenario: message_content is denied. First boot after the denial: emit_degrade_notices fires, the finding lands in the in-process ring, the latch persists 'message_content' to a settings row. The dyno restarts an hour later for any reason. The latch still reads 'message_content', so emit_degrade_notices returns False and records nothing; the ring starts empty. From that boot onward the bot runs permanently degraded with zero findings anywhere, zero notices, and a green /ready — and the design says that is correct behaviour.
defects.successor_recommendation: Separate 'do not spam' from 'do not record'. The successor should re-assert every active degraded state on every boot into a durable store and a status surface, and use the latch only to suppress the outbound ALERT, never the record. A degraded state must be a standing fact you can query, not an event you had to be watching for.

lanes.headline: The golden corpus is not a proof about the shipping bot: on the "actual" side every wire byte is produced by `rendered_panel_payload()` in sb/adapters/parity/transport.py, a serializer used by nothing but the parity adapter and its own tests, while production installs a completely separate `DiscordPanelPresenter` (sb/app/panel_host.py:66) that nothing in CI exercises — so parity compares old-bot discord.py bytes against a hand-maintained model of discord.py. On top of that, 38/533 goldens assert literally nothing (0 calls, 0 events, empty db_delta), 165/183 rendered component custom_ids are never clicked by any case, 36/533 pin a refusal as the expected behaviour, and the "depth floor" that guards all of it (check_parity_depth, EXIT=0) never touches a bot at all — it is a self-consistency check over three committed files whose settings dimension is vacuous for 49/49 subsystems. What IS worth keeping: the db_delta effect assertion (real TRUNCATE→snapshot→diff over pg_tables), the F-003 replayed-count==golden-count denominator assert, check_runtime_smoke's real composition-root reachability boot, the check_no_skip single-entry-seam fence (the cog-portability enabler), and the 413-command/265-custom_id compat pin.

strengths.claim: A golden's db_delta is a REAL persisted-effect assertion, not bytes: capture_case TRUNCATEs every public table with RESTART IDENTITY, applies fixture SQL, snapshots every row of every table from pg_tables before and after, and diffs at row level. 471 of 533 goldens (533 minus the 62 with empty db_delta) carry a non-empty db_delta, and dispositions do not empty a single one of them (62 empty before, 62 empty after — measured).
strengths.contradicts: The reading that a golden is a screenshot/byte pin. It is both: bytes AND a full-database row delta. The prior audit's framing of goldens as photographs is right about the render half and wrong about the DB half.
strengths.prevents_failure: a command that still renders the correct copy but silently stops writing its row (award granted in the embed, never persisted) — the render diff stays green, the db_delta goes red
strengths.guard_population: every table returned by `SELECT tablename FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname='public'` on the live replay database — non-empty by construction once migrations have run, and it CANNOT degrade to a model: there is no fake DB seam, the run errors out (measured: gate EXIT=1, 'asyncpg is not installed') rather than false-greening.
strengths.successor_recommendation: Keep this exact primitive in the successor's effect layer: per-case truncate + full-schema snapshot + row-level delta, with volatile columns scrubbed BY NAME (dbsnap.py:23-29) rather than by shape. It is the only assertion in either repo that proves a write happened.

strengths.claim: tools/run_golden_parity.py asserts replayed_count == golden_count per ported subsystem, so a golden file that fails case reconstruction reds the gate instead of silently shrinking the checked set. This is the direct fix for the 'invisible golden' class and it is the ONE place in the parity system where the denominator is the artifact on disk rather than something enumerated from a live object.
strengths.quote:
denominator_mismatches = 0
    for name in ported:

strengths.prevents_failure: a golden whose case_id is missing, unreconstructable, or collides with an earlier file vanishing from the replayed set with no signal — the gate reporting GREEN over fewer cases than exist
strengths.guard_population: the 533 golden .json files on disk across 50 ported subsystem dirs (49 + kernel), counted by `_golden_counts()` glob — non-empty and independently derived from the replay path, which is the whole point.
strengths.successor_recommendation: Make this the general rule in the successor, not a one-off: every gate states its denominator's SOURCE and asserts that the number it checked equals the number that exists. The bug it fixes (two code paths counting the same thing and never compared) is the single most repeated defect class across both repos.

strengths.claim: check_runtime_smoke boots the real composition root headlessly (the same code path as sb.app.main / verify_boot, not a re-implementation) and asserts every manifest ref resolves to a real callable, every PanelRef names a registered panel, and every armed subscriber names a KNOWN_EVENTS event bound to a real callable. Measured over 49 manifests, 1327 dispatch targets, 314 panels, 6 roster modules; EXIT=0.

Non-empty, and derived from the real loader — but note it deliberately leaves the presenter uninstalled when discord is absent (sb/app/panel_host.py:61-62), so it proves route EXISTENCE, never route OUTPUT.

Extend it with one assertion it currently lacks: every registered panel component custom_id must resolve to a handler — that is the 165-never-clicked hole (R5-D03) closed statically instead of by writing 165 click goldens.

   `@tree.command`, `@app_commands.command`, `tree.interaction_check`,
   `bot.add_view`, `@bot.listen`) may appear ONLY under the sanctioned

strengths.area: compat contract — the legacy surface pin
strengths.claim: compat/compat-frozen.json pins 413 command rows across 46 subsystems, 265 legacy custom_ids, 49 subsystem keys, 23 event-payload field sets and 17 legacy AI task ids; check_compat_frozen derives the same set from manifest.snapshot.json and reds on any drift (EXIT=0 measured). The snapshot it derives from is itself recompiled from source in CI ('Compile + snapshot drift (P9 recompile-parity)', named-gates.yml:65), so the chain source -> snapshot -> pin is closed, and `golden-parity` and `check_compat_frozen` are BOTH confirmed required status checks on main via the rulesets API.
strengths.prevents_failure: silently renaming or dropping a legacy command name/alias or a persisted-panel custom_id — which breaks every button on every message already posted in the guild, and every user's muscle memory, with no runtime error anywhere
strengths.guard_population: 413 command rows + 265 custom_ids + 49 subsystem keys derived from the committed manifest snapshot. Non-empty and measured. IT IS A MODEL in one respect: it compares two committed files, so it proves the DECLARED surface is stable, never that the running bot serves it — that gap is covered by check_runtime_smoke's W1/W2 (R5-S03), and only in combination are the two worth anything.
strengths.successor_recommendation: This is the cog-portability contract the successor needs, and it is the highest-value artifact in either repo for the owner's stated goal. Keep it, keep the CODEOWNERS routing on the pin, and add the missing third link: a runtime assertion that every pinned command name and custom_id is actually registered after boot.

strengths.claim: The three owner-ruled 'old bot vs new bot differs forever' classes are applied SYMMETRICALLY to both the stored golden and the fresh capture before diffing, so an accepted class cannot become a one-sided blind spot through which a real behaviour change smuggles itself. The encoding lives as data in parity.yml (`dispositions:`) with the mechanism in one module; the goldens themselves are never rewritten.
strengths.quote:
The three owner-accepted "old bot vs new bot output differs forever" classes
are applied HERE, at replay-diff time, to BOTH the stored golden and the
fresh capture — symmetrically, so the diff stays honest for every other

cannot smuggle itself through (both docs get the same treatment).
strengths.prevents_failure: a known-acceptable difference being handled by editing the golden (corpus corruption) or by a one-sided filter that also hides unrelated regressions on the same surface
strengths.guard_population: every replayed case: both documents pass through apply_dispositions() at sb/adapters/parity/runner.py:513-514. Non-empty. BUT the population it REMOVES is large and must be reported with it — 432 of 1173 outbound calls (37%) and 9 kernel tables + 2 kernel events from every non-kernel golden (see R5-D10).
strengths.successor_recommendation: Keep the symmetric-transform pattern and the data/mechanism split. Add the guard it lacks: a hard ceiling on what fraction of assertions a disposition may erase, printed on every run, so 'accepted difference' cannot quietly grow into 'we no longer check the output'.

strengths.claim: An outbound effect the transport does not model is recorded as a GAP and raises during capture AND during replay (replay_case calls capture_case), so a golden can never silently under-record. In the replay driver the raise surfaces as 'replay crashed' and reds the case (run_golden_parity.py:107-108) rather than passing.

strengths.claim: check_parity_depth R1 refuses any exemption whose reason does not begin with one of 12 declared reason classes ('never a bare flaky'). defects.claim: Every wire byte on the ACTUAL side of a golden diff is produced by `rendered_panel_payload()`, defined once in sb/adapters/parity/transport.py:242 and imported by exactly three places, all of them parity: transport.py itself, tests/unit/parity_adapter/test_replay_adapter.py and tests/unit/parity_adapter/test_utility_capture.py. defects.contradicts: parity/README.md:16-18 — 'Inputs are synthetic gateway payloads fed to the real `ConnectionState` parser (`parity/harness/world.py`), so every object the bot touches is a genuine discord.py model.' That was true of the OLD capture side. It is FALSE of the new replay side, and the README was never amended. defects.claim: 38 of 533 goldens (7.1%) assert literally nothing after dispositions: zero outbound calls, zero events, empty db_delta. All 38 are slash cases, i.e. 38 of the 66 goldens containing a slash step (58%). Example verbatim, parity/goldens/ai/sweep_slash_ai_status.json in full: case_id sweep.slash_ai_status, `"db_delta": {}`, `"calls": []`. Only 28 of 66 slash goldens record any outbound call at all.

Also contradicts the audit's framing that a golden is 'a photograph of a panel' — 38 of them are a photograph of a blank wall.
defects.failure_scenario: A user runs /ai status in the guild and Discord shows 'The application did not respond'. The successor bot registers the command and returns nothing at all. sweep.slash_ai_status replays green — 0 calls expected, 0 calls produced — and so do the other 37. golden-parity reports full parity for a slash surface that is completely dead.

Add a minimum-assertion floor to the harness: every case must assert at least one of (an outbound call, an event, a db row) or carry an explicit classed exemption. Then re-mint or retire all 38 — most likely they encode a genuine capture-side blind spot in the slash interaction-response path, which is a bug to fix, not a golden to keep.

defects.area: golden corpus — panels are photographed, never actuated
defects.claim: Across the whole 533-golden corpus, 183 distinct component custom_ids are RENDERED but only 23 are ever clicked, and 5 of those 23 do not appear in the rendered set (normalized session ids), so 165 of 183 rendered controls (90%) are never actuated by any case. Only 42 of 533 goldens (7.9%) contain a click step at all; 485 of 533 are single-step. The corpus has 475 command steps, 66 slash steps, 86 click steps and 6 modal steps.
defects.contradicts: parity/COVERAGE.md:13 — 'Persistent-panel components (custom_ids) | 60 | 64 | **94%**'. That 94% counts a custom_id as covered when it is merely RENDERED inside a captured component tree (coverage.py methodology: 'custom_id rendered in a captured component tree'). Measured against actuation the real figure is 18/183 = 10%. The doc and the corpus disagree by an order of magnitude.
defects.failure_scenario: The successor renders the settings hub panel with all its buttons and its handler table is misrouted, so every button raises on click. The panel's render golden matches byte-for-byte — the components array is identical — and golden-parity is green. The first owner to click 'Edit channel' gets an interaction failure. This is confirmed for 165 of the 183 controls the corpus draws.
defects.successor_recommendation: Rendering a control and handling it are two assertions; the corpus only ever makes the first. In the successor, a panel is not covered until every control it renders has been actuated at least once and the result asserted — enforce it statically (every registered custom_id resolves to a handler, cheaply, in the check_runtime_smoke boot) plus dynamically for the controls that mutate state.

defects.area: golden corpus — refusals pinned as behaviour

defects.area: check_parity_depth — proves nothing about a bot
defects.claim: check_parity_depth never boots or contacts anything: it reads parity/goldens/*/*.json, manifest.snapshot.json and parity.yml, and it says so in its own docstring. Measured on this machine with no discord.py, no asyncpg, no Postgres and no bot: EXIT=0. Its R3 ratchet compares counts computed from committed golden FILES against committed numbers in parity.yml, so the ratchet can only ever fall if someone deletes golden files.

defects.failure_scenario: A successor branch guts every handler in sb/domain/ to `pass`. check_parity_depth still exits 0 — the golden files on disk are unchanged, the manifest snapshot is unchanged, the ratchet counts are unchanged. Anyone treating the named gate's first step as evidence of behavioural depth is reading a checksum of files nobody touched.
defects.successor_recommendation: Keep it, rename it, and stop billing it as depth: it is a corpus-hygiene linter (rows pair with dirs, exemptions are classed, counts are monotone). The successor needs a genuinely separate depth measure that reads the live registries and the replay result, not the corpus's self-description.

Nobody learns the surface is gone. The denominator moved and the numerator moved with it.
defects.successor_recommendation: Never let a live-enumerated set be the denominator of a regression check. The corpus is the denominator; the live surface is a second, separately-asserted set; the gate compares them. run_golden_parity's F-003 fix is the pattern — port that, delete parity/run.py's check leg or make it fail loudly on unmatched goldens.

defects.claim: Applying the three ruled dispositions to the corpus removes 432 of 1173 outbound calls from the diff (37%) and strips 9 kernel tables (idempotency_keys, event_outbox, audit_log, sb_due_queue, sb_drafts, sb_quarantine, sb_invariant_sweep_log, sb_credential_rotation, ai_decision_audit) plus 2 kernel events (audit.action_recorded, command.dispatched) from the db_delta of every non-kernel golden. 45 goldens end up asserting zero outbound calls after dispositions, up from 38 before.

Separately, audit_log and event_outbox writes are dropped from every non-kernel golden's db_delta, so a subsystem that stops writing its audit trail is invisible outside the 'kernel' band.

Where a disposition exists because the two bots genuinely differ forever, the successor should assert the NEW behaviour positively somewhere else — the kernel band does this correctly for the spine and is the model to copy.

The clock base is position-independent; the in-memory state is not, and the loader docstring says so explicitly. The README's determinism section and the loader's docstring cannot both be right.

The DB is truncated per case (dbsnap.reset_database) but the process's in-memory caches are not.
defects.successor_recommendation: Per-case isolation must cover process memory the way it already covers the database. In the successor, in-memory conversation/session state belongs behind an injectable store that the harness resets per case — the same fix the sweep's own EXCLUDED_COMMANDS entries already call for ('unseeded private RNG', 'real-TTL in-memory cache'), which parity/cases/sweep.py:64-72 labels 'REBUILD DESIGN INPUT'.

honest_nulls: I could not run the parity harness end to end. asyncpg and discord.py are absent and the lane is read-only, so `tools/run_golden_parity.py --gate` reached the binding probe and stopped (EXIT=1, 'Postgres unavailable: asyncpg is not installed'). Everything I claim about replay behaviour is read from source plus static analysis of the 533 committed goldens; I never observed a green or red replay of a single case. In particular I did NOT verify the workflow's claim of 533/533 green, and I could not check whether the 38 zero-assertion goldens would replay green in practice or crash on a transport gap first.

I could not establish whether the 5 commits touching disbot/ since the pinned oracle sha changed any captured behaviour. Measured: menno420/superbot HEAD (5e3a667b) is 1286 commits past the parity.yml source sha 7f7628e1, of which 5 touch disbot/ (11 files, +419/-2). Whether any of those 11 files is on a path a golden exercises is unknown — establishing it needs the old bot booted, which this repo cannot do (R5-D09).

I did not verify claim (2) of the prompt in its strongest form ('a photograph of a panel scores as FULL parity') for a specific named panel end to end. What I measured is the corpus-wide actuation ratio (165/183 rendered custom_ids never clicked) and the single-step ratio (485/533). I did not trace one panel from render golden through its handler table to prove the handler could be deleted with the gate staying green.

I could not determine whether the 4 `needs_discord`-skipped tests in tests/unit/app/test_cut1_surfaces.py run in ANY CI job. named-gates.yml code-quality installs only pytest+pyyaml, and golden-parity installs requirements.lock (which presumably has discord.py) but runs only tests/integration and tests/e2e, not tests/unit. I read the workflow files; I did not fetch an actual CI run's logs to confirm the skip count in CI. The local measurement (4 skipped, 44 skipped suite-wide) is real; its CI counterpart is inferred.

parity.yml's `depth.ratchet` rows: I confirmed R3 compares committed counts against counts computed from golden files on disk, and that check_parity_depth passes. I did NOT audit whether any individual ratchet row is set below its current coverage (a slack ratchet), which would make R3 non-binding for that subsystem even where the denominator is non-empty. That needs a per-subsystem row-vs-measured comparison I did not spend the budget on.

No row was dropped for space. I wrote 8 strengths and 12 defects; the defect cap was reached and one further measured item (oracle drift since the pin) was demoted to the honest null above rather than cut silently.

For question (4) — what a golden CAN legitimately prove — my answer is reasoned, not measured, and belongs here rather than in a row: a golden legitimately proves (a) that a named EFFECT occurred (the db_delta half, R5-S01), (b) that a previously-observed output has not changed, PROVIDED the actual side is produced by the same code path production uses (which R5-D01 shows is false today), and (c) that a case that used to be reachable still is. It cannot prove correctness, cannot prove coverage, and must never be minted from the artifact under test. The safe contract is: goldens are a REGRESSION net over a surface some other layer has already proven correct — never the acceptance oracle for a rebuild.

For question (5) — the replacement layers — this is design, not evidence, so it is stated here rather than as rows. STRUCTURAL: manifest compiles from source in CI and the compat pin (413 commands / 265 custom_ids) matches it, both directions asserted (keep R5-S05, add the runtime link). UNIT: pure domain logic with no Discord and no DB — but the suite must not be able to pass 3648 tests with neither dependency installed while claiming to cover adapters; adapter tests that skip without discord.py must fail the job instead. CONTRACT: one shared wire-serializer that both the production presenter and any harness call, fenced by an AST check so a second one cannot exist (this is R5-D01's fix and the highest-value single change). JOURNEY: multi-step flows that assert an effect at every step, with per-case isolation covering process memory as well as the database (R5-D12). REACHABILITY: check_runtime_smoke's W1/W2/W3 extended so every RENDERED custom_id must resolve to a handler — that closes the 165/183 hole statically (R5-D03). EFFECT: keep dbsnap's truncate/snapshot/diff verbatim, and make a case that asserts no effect and no output a RED (R5-D02). REAL-GUILD: a non-empty, counted, signed registry with a floor — an empty one must red, not report OK (R5-D07). The common rule under all seven: every gate names its denominator's source and reds when that denominator is empty, because four separate guards in this estate are currently green over the empty set.

lanes.lane: R6 — convergence, inversions, and what both audits missed
lanes.method_note:
All commands run read-only from the given pins (superbot 5e3a667b, superbot-next d5f66dc2, fleet-manager caa6cd2a). Real exit codes, no `$?` after a pipe.

lanes.headline: superbot-next is a PORT of superbot, not an independent convergence — and on the one axis that decides whether guards work, superbot is the donor, not next. Superbot's enforcement locus is not its workflow file (15 of 45 checkers appear there) but pytest: 44 of 45 checkers are driven from tests/ as libraries behind blocking, zero-tolerance, stale-detecting invariant tests. superbot-next inverted that — 24 checkers in a `set -e` workflow loop over 273 test files — and three of its flagship "required, no-expiry" gates are green over an empty or unsigned population. The third bot should take next's declarative panel/manifest kernel (20,486 LOC, 13.6% of sb/) and superbot's guard architecture, and must never inherit a ratchet whose baseline is {} .

strengths.claim: Superbot's real enforcement locus is pytest, not the workflow step list: 44 of 45 scripts/check_*.py are referenced from at least one file under tests/, while only 15 of 45 appear in any .github/workflows/*.yml. The checkers are LIBRARIES; the gate is `pytest tests/ -v -n auto` at code-quality.yml:279 with no continue-on-error. I read the pattern end-to-end in 1 of the 44 (test_command_reachability.py) and confirmed a second exists (test_settings_reachability.py). The invariant loads the checker in-process, ratchets against `_BASELINE = frozenset()` (zero tolerated gaps) and carries test_baseline_has_no_stale_entries so the baseline can only shrink.
strengths.quote:
It drives ``scripts/check_command_reachability.py`` (the static checker) and
**ratchets against a recorded baseline** (Q-0105 warn-first): the pre-existing
orphan-cog gaps are tolerated, but any *new* unreachable member command fails —
which is what makes "every command findable" un-regressable while the per-cog
audit follow-on sessions clear the baseline.
...
_BASELINE: frozenset[tuple[str, str]] = frozenset()
strengths.contradicts: MY OWN MID-LANE FINDING, stated loudly: I first counted 15 of 45 checkers in CI and 0 runners for check_command_reachability / check_settings_reachability anywhere in .github/ or .claude/, and was about to file 'superbot's reachability enforcement runs nowhere' as a defect. That reading is REFUTED — I then found tests/unit/invariants/test_command_reachability.py and test_settings_reachability.py. It also contradicts any rebuild plan that treats superbot-next as the reachability/enforcement donor and superbot as the undisciplined predecessor: superbot's zero-tolerance, stale-detecting ratchet over the real command surface is strictly stronger than next's navigation_golden over a conftest-emptied registry.
strengths.prevents_failure: a member-tier command ships in a cog that no !help click-path reaches — the exact gap the owner reported ('the general cog is completely unfindable from the help menu')
strengths.guard_population: Every prefix command discovered by AST over disbot/ (214 prefix commands / 75 reachable per the 2026-06-23 session record). It CANNOT be empty in the dangerous direction: an empty command set produces no gaps but also no bot, and the sibling test_baseline_has_no_stale_entries fires if a recorded gap disappears. This is the artifact (the source tree), not a hand-built model — unlike the help-reachability invariant next to it.
strengths.simpler_than_counterpart: One 276-line test file plus a checker library replaces next's separate workflow YAML loop; the ratchet lives in the same file as the assertion, so it cannot drift from it.
strengths.successor_recommendation: Adopt this shape wholesale in bot three: checker = importable library, gate = pytest invariant, tolerance = an explicit frozenset that starts empty, plus a stale-entry test so the tolerance can only shrink. It is the only mechanism I found in either repo that makes a guard un-loosenable without a visible diff.

class NavigationSpec:
    """Serializable — kills the closure-backed BackTarget/chain_back stacks.
    Every route is re-resolved and capability-checked at click time; parents
    are rebuilt fresh, never captured."""

    parent: PanelRef | None = None              # [S]
    home_hub: str = FOLLOW_PARENT               # [S] the routing RULE, not a captured value

strengths.contradicts: The framing that superbot-next 'merely restated' superbot's patterns. Generalizes the proven shape of ``navigation_stack._locks`` so any future
realtime / event-driven cog (counting, tournaments, matchmaking,
reaction games, limited-quantity drops) can serialize its hot-path
mutation under a narrow, per-scope lock without growing yet another
bespoke lock dictionary.

the lock guards the validate + mutate + persist phase; Discord I/O

They add four lines to layers.yaml with a rationale sentence, and the gate greens permanently — no count rises, no ledger entry, no expiry, and nothing ever detects that the entry is still there after the import is removed. defects.successor_recommendation: Bot three: allowlists must carry a COUNT baseline (next's shape), a stale-entry test (superbot's own test_command_reachability.py:test_baseline_has_no_stale_entries proves the pattern exists in-repo and was simply not applied here), and an expiry date. Every mechanism needed already exists in these two repos; nobody combined them.

defects.area: SHARED DEFECT — guards prove registration, never usefulness
defects.claim: Both repos' strongest reachability/wiring guards assert that a thing is REGISTERED, and neither asserts that it DOES anything. In superbot-next, check_runtime_smoke's W2 rule is explicit: every PanelRef must name a panel_id registered in the registry. That is exactly why 153 of 314 compiled panels (49%) carry zero actions and the gate is green at EXIT=0. In superbot the same shape appears one level up: reachability is defined as 'some owning subsystem is homed under a top-level hub and has a help-discovery path' — a property of the routing graph, not of what the panel renders.
defects.quote:
W2 panel-graph    — every PanelRef names a panel_id REGISTERED in the
                      panel registry after ``register_manifest_panels`` (the
                      band-1 replay's exact LookupError class).
defects.contradicts: The prior live audit's already-settled 314/153/49% figures, which this row re-reads as a GUARD-DESIGN defect rather than a content defect: the zero-action panels are not an oversight that slipped past the gates, they are precisely what the gates were built to permit. Also contradicts R6-S03's own strength claim in the honest direction — check_runtime_smoke is the best guard in either repo AND it is structurally blind to the largest measured defect in the same repo.
defects.failure_scenario: A user clicks through the help hub to a subsystem panel. It renders — title, embed, the injected nav row — and there is nothing else on it: no button, no select, nothing that does the thing the panel is named after. He clicks Back. Every gate in both repos is green: the panel is registered (W2), it is reachable from a homed subsystem (superbot's invariant), and its nav row is injected (render.py:606). 153 of 314 panels in superbot-next are in exactly this state.
defects.successor_recommendation: Bot three needs one new invariant neither repo has: every registered panel must expose >=1 action/selector OR declare `terminal: true` with a reason, gated at compile time. Add it to the manifest compiler so it cannot be added later as an allowlist. This single rule kills the largest measured defect class in the estate.

defects.area: AI task admission — INVERSION, superbot is more correct
defects.claim: Replacing superbot's closed AITask enum (17 members, disbot/core/runtime/ai/contracts.py:16-42) with a runtime registry traded a static guarantee for a boot-order dependency. The kernel seeds exactly 1 of the 17 frozen legacy task ids ('general.nl_answer'); the other 16 depend on a domain band's ai_tasks module being imported. I counted 13 register_task call sites across 10 sb/domain/*/ai_tasks.py modules. On top of that the admission check itself is bypassable: gateway.py:255 skips it entirely when provider_override is passed.
defects.quote:
The kernel itself seeds only the domain-agnostic fallback task
(``general.nl_answer``): every other shipped id waits for its band.
defects.contradicts: sb/kernel/ai/gateway.py:1-9, whose docstring states 'the task id must be REGISTERED (:mod:`sb.kernel.ai.tasks`; replaces the closed-enum guarantee)' — the code at line 255 reads `if provider_override is None and not tasks.task_registered(task_id)`, so the stated guarantee has a hole the docstring does not mention. It also contradicts the framing of superbot-next as the architecture donor: the closed enum made an unregistered task UNREPRESENTABLE at import time; the registry converts that into a silent runtime degradation.
defects.failure_scenario: A user asks the bot a BTD6 question. sb/domain/btd6/ai_tasks.py was not imported at boot (a band not yet loaded, a plugin not installed, an import ordering change). The gateway resolves task 'btd6.answer', finds it unregistered, and returns a degraded AIResponse with reason 'task_unregistered:btd6.answer'. The user gets a generic non-answer, never an error; the metric label records the degradation but nothing reds. Under the shipped closed enum this state could not exist — the id was a member of the type.
defects.new_failure_class: Silent capability loss from module import order, replacing a compile-time impossibility.
defects.successor_recommendation: Keep the registry (domains minting their own tasks is right for cog-portability), but add the missing guard: a boot-time or CI assertion that every id in LEGACY_TASK_IDS — and every id any manifest references — is registered after the composition root finishes. next already has the right place for it (check_runtime_smoke's W1 ref-graph). Remove or narrow the provider_override bypass; only sb/kernel/ai/evals.py uses it (2 call sites).

defects.area: SHARED DEFECT family — guards that print the finding and exit 0
defects.claim: 4 of superbot-next's 28 checkers print a REAL, specific finding and still exit 0, so the ci.yml `set -e` loop passes over them: check_settle_once (names an unlocked concurrency race in karma), check_rotation_due ('6 rotation(s) due', including two ROOT owner-prompt tokens), check_doc_cites (a doc cites lines 36-63 of a 56-line file), check_verified_live (0 records). Superbot has the same family via continue-on-error (R6-D03). Neither repo distinguishes 'clean' from 'findings, tolerated'.
defects.quote: KNOWN-RISK (ledgered, NOT safe) sb/domain/karma/ops.py:139 [_record_give -> karma.record_give] — cooldown/cap reads are UNLOCKED plain SELECTs (store.recent_grant_count / grants_given_since) and credit_karma is an unconditioned upsert (sb/domain/karma/ops.py:138-229): two racing grants from the same giver both pass the window checks and both land — the cooldown/cap can over-admit under concurrency; needs a FOR-UPDATE anchor row or advisory fence (the ensure_and_get_economy shape)
defects.contradicts: The same run's summary line, 'settle_once: 36 roots — RC:15 CAS:9 CW:10 allowlisted:1 known-risk:1 warn:0' followed by 'check_settle_once: OK' and EXIT=0. The checker's own output says NOT safe and its exit code says OK. A session grading this repo by exit codes — which is what ci.yml does — records 28 of 28 green and never sees the sentence above.
defects.failure_scenario: Two users (or one user double-clicking) fire karma grants from the same giver within the same window. Both handlers run store.recent_grant_count as unlocked plain SELECTs, both see a count under the cap, both pass, and credit_karma upserts twice. The daily cap is exceeded, the cooldown is bypassed, and the karma ledger is wrong. CI was green for every commit that shipped it, and the checker built to find exactly this printed it and exited 0.
defects.successor_recommendation: Bot three: a checker has exactly two exit codes and 'ledgered known-risk' is not one of them. Route tolerated findings through a counted ratchet baseline (the escape-hatch shape) so the number can only shrink, and make the summary line machine-parsed by CI rather than a human-read string. Fix the karma race with superbot's scope_locks Validate/Mutate/Apply pattern (R6-S08).

defects.area: what 'architecture donor' actually buys — INVERSION on size
defects.claim: The novel architecture in superbot-next is 20,486 LOC. Counted (find + wc -l, __pycache__ excluded): sb/ total 150,328 LOC, of which sb/domain is 111,929 (74.5%) and sb/kernel is 20,486 (13.6%). superbot's disbot/ is 243,961 LOC. So superbot-next carries 61.6% of the shipped runtime's line count, and the part that is genuinely new design — the kernel the rebuild plan treats as the donor — is 8.4% of the shipped bot. The remaining 130k lines are ports (54 basename-matched pairs measured, 8 at ≥0.90 similarity, 1 md5-identical).
defects.quote:
"""AI gateway (K10) — the single never-raises chokepoint for provider calls.

Ported from shipped ``disbot/core/runtime/ai/gateway.py`` @7f7628e1 onto
the kernel seams.
defects.contradicts: The prior planning's treatment of superbot-next as 'the architecture donor', which reads as though adopting it delivers most of a bot. It delivers ~20k lines of kernel plus a re-homed copy of superbot's domain logic, and leaves 93,633 LOC of shipped disbot behaviour (243,961 − 150,328) with no counterpart in next at the current pin. It also contradicts my own §1 brief: the AI gateway is not a convergence at all — 584 vs 583 lines, whole functions moved verbatim.
defects.failure_scenario: A rebuild session is told 'start from superbot-next's architecture' and budgets accordingly. Partway through it discovers that 49% of the panels it inherited do nothing (settled), that 74.5% of what it inherited is ported superbot domain code it could have ported directly, and that ~94k LOC of shipped behaviour — the parts users actually use in the live bot — has no next-side counterpart and must still be carried across from superbot. The plan's size estimate is wrong by roughly the size of the original bot.
defects.successor_recommendation: State the split explicitly in the rebuild plan: superbot-next contributes a 20,486-LOC kernel (manifest compiler, namespace oracle, panel render engine, interaction fence) and a proven port PROCEDURE (533 goldens, 49 subsystems). Everything else is a carry-across from superbot that bot three must do again regardless of which repo it starts from. Decide on the kernel, not on the repo.

defects.area: documentation baseline — INVERSION the owner named himself
defects.claim: On the axis the owner explicitly called his quality baseline, superbot is ahead by an order of magnitude: 863 .md files under superbot/docs versus 92 under superbot-next/docs (9.4x), and 1060 test_*.py versus 273 (3.9x). superbot also carries a 10-file architecture_rules/ rule corpus (layers.yaml, mutation_owners.yaml, canonical_helpers.yaml and 5 exception registries) that has no superbot-next equivalent — next's rules live inside the 27 checker scripts as Python constants.
defects.quote:
# Mutation ownership rules for SuperBot.
#
# Each domain has exactly one canonical mutation service. Direct database
# writes (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) outside utils/db/ and the owning service
# are flagged as violations.
#
# The canonical write path for all domains is:
#   caller → *_mutation.py service → utils.db.[submodule] → pool.execute()
#
# pool.execute() and other raw db primitives are ONLY allowed inside utils/db/.
defects.contradicts: Any disposition that treats superbot as history to be archived and superbot-next as the doc/test donor. The owner said on 2026-09-01 that documentation was 'especially true in /superbot before the EAP was announced'; the counts confirm it at the current pins. Honest limit: I counted files, not quality, and superbot's 863 includes the EAP-era process docs the owner was NOT praising. Separately, mutation_owners.yaml is the 'one-owner-per-write-path' convergence candidate this lane was asked about — superbot ORIGINATED it as an externalized rule file read by check_architecture.py and context_map.py, and superbot-next did NOT carry it across in any form I could find (grep for 'one owner'/'write_owner'/'mutation' across sb/kernel, tools/ and docs/ found no equivalent registry).
defects.failure_scenario: Bot three is seeded from superbot-next as the 'clean' repo. A maintainer adds a cog and looks for the doc that says where writes must go. superbot-next has 92 docs and no externalized mutation-ownership rule file; superbot has that rule as machine-readable YAML consumed by a blocking CI gate. The maintainer writes a direct pool.execute() in the cog, no rule file exists to point at, and the reviewer has nothing to cite.
defects.successor_recommendation: Carry superbot's externalized-rules pattern (architecture_rules/*.yaml as data, checkers as readers) into bot three, and carry mutation_owners.yaml's one-owner-per-write-path declaration specifically — it is the cleanest statement of that invariant anywhere in the estate and it did not survive into superbot-next. Seed the doc corpus from superbot's pre-EAP subset, not from next's 92.

honest_nulls: COULD NOT EXECUTE superbot's two reachability checkers or ANY superbot test. `python3 scripts/check_command_reachability.py` EXIT=1 (ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'discord', raised from disbot/core/runtime/__init__.py:53 → persistent_views.py:32); `python3 scripts/check_settings_reachability.py` EXIT=1 (same, via disbot/utils/ui_constants.py:3). DID NOT BOOT EITHER BOT. No claim here rests on live Discord behaviour. superbot-next's checkers I ran are the repo's own committed gates at the current pin; superbot's three that ran bare (check_architecture, check_audit_seam, check_consistency) are stdlib+PyYAML only. VERIFIED BUT DROPPED FOR ROW BUDGET — each is a real artifact-population guard in superbot-next that ran EXIT=0 over a non-empty population: check_data_lifecycle (81 stores), check_metric_cardinality (51 families), check_credential_lifecycle (14 credentials / 10 worker fields), check_sim_gate (1618 [A] assignments), check_slash_cap (49 manifests / 413 commands), check_migrations (57 migrations), check_symbol_shadowing, check_egress, check_cost_posture.
