strengths.contradicts: The same checker prints a fully specified live money race in karma and exits 0 (R2-D10/R6-D08). One file simultaneously holds the estate's best excuse-expiry mechanism and its clearest print-and-pass. The lesson a rebuild must take is that these are independent properties: expiry without fail-closed is a well-maintained list of things nobody fixes.
strengths.prevents_failure: a stale exemption row silently re-covering a NEW violation that happens to match the same key
strengths.guard_population: 36 classified money roots at this pin (RC:15 CAS:9 CW:10, allowlisted:1, known-risk:1). Non-empty and derived from the real tree, not a model.
strengths.successor_recommendation: Adopt globally: every allowlist/exemption/baseline entry must red when it no longer matches anything, AND the checker must exit nonzero on its own findings. Cost: near zero to add; the real cost is the backlog it surfaces on day one.

strengths.claim: The repo already invented the correct answer to its own biggest blind spot: parity/goldens/kernel/ documents are EXEMPTED from the kernel-surface-drift strip so the audit/outbox/dispatch spine is diffed somewhere instead of nowhere. The design is right and the population is 4 files — MEASURED: exactly 3 of 533 goldens carry an audit_log delta and all 3 are kernel-band; corpus-wide they assert 1 distinct mutation_type (xp_awarded).
strengths.quote:
KERNEL-BAND documents (``subsystem == "kernel"`` — the parity.yml
    `kernel` coverage home's own minted goldens, D-0075) skip the
    kernel-surface-drift drop entirely: the disposition exists because
    IMPORTED old-bot captures structurally never carry the new kernel's
    spine surfaces, but the kernel band's whole point is to PIN those
    surfaces (audit_log / event_outbox / command.dispatched bytes) so
    kernel drift goes red somewhere.
strengths.contradicts: M9-S03's 'audit is a property of the mutation engine … 175 of 175 CompoundOpSpecs carry a non-empty audit_verb (100%)' reads as proof the audit spine works. Measured: the compiler proves 175 non-empty STRINGS; the acceptance oracle proves 1 audit ROW, for 1 op, in 3 documents. 'audit_verb declared' and 'audit row written' are different claims and the estate has been quoting the first as the second.
strengths.prevents_failure: kernel spine regression (audit row not written, outbox row not enqueued) going undetected because every domain golden strips those tables from both sides of the diff
strengths.guard_population: parity/goldens/kernel/ — 4 files (kernel_audited_prefix_command, kernel_audited_modal_submit, kernel_denied_prefix_command, kernel_slash_dispatch_trace) against 175 registered CompoundOpSpecs. Non-empty but 2.3% of the ops it purports to cover.
strengths.successor_recommendation: Invert the default instead of the exception: the kernel spine is diffed on EVERY case, and a domain case that legitimately cannot carry it names that surface in an expiring exemption row (F-S05's shape). Cost: re-minting the corpus against the new bot once — which is exactly the work byte-parity was chosen to avoid, so this is a real, ownable trade, not a free win.

strengths.claim: pending_handler is a first-class primitive for 'declared surface, honest refusal, never silent' — a registered handler returning Reply(BLOCKED, message). It is genuinely better than a dead button. Counted 4 live uses in the ref table (admin.cogmgr_deploy_pending, admin.reload_all_pending, btd6.cmd_strat_pending, btd6.strat_pending_view) out of 1947 registered refs.
strengths.contradicts: R3-D8 files the Cog Manager's pending buttons purely as a regression. The PRIMITIVE is right (the user gets a stated refusal, not a spinner); the defect is that nothing counts its uses — see F-D12. Preserving the primitive and adding the counter are the same PR.
strengths.prevents_failure: a declared control that silently does nothing when clicked (the user cannot tell 'not built yet' from 'broken')
strengths.guard_population: 4 of 1947 registered refs today. Nothing bounds it: the same primitive satisfies W1 (resolves to a callable), W2 (panel registered), O1 (has a _REF_TABLE entry) and O2 (referenced by a panel) at any count up to 1947.
strengths.successor_recommendation: Keep it and ratchet it: a committed per-subsystem pending count that may only fall, printed in the boot summary and in the user-facing help. Cost: one baseline file plus a boot line.

strengths.claim: check_runtime_smoke's W1/W2 are a genuine runtime wiring floor over the real registries — W1 requires every reachable ref to resolve to a CALLABLE, W2 requires every PanelRef to name a registered panel_id — and the digest confirms both fire on injected positives. Preserve it. But read what it proves: 'callable' is the entire assertion, so a tree of 1947 no-op coroutines is indistinguishable from a working bot. 2 tools reuse the same headless composition-boot pattern (check_runtime_smoke, check_orphan_pendings).
strengths.contradicts: M11-S02 calls this 'the strongest proof layer in the repo' and R3-S5/R6-S03 read it as refuting the empty-population framing. Both are right about the population and wrong about the ceiling: R6-D06 already names the shape ('guards prove registration, never usefulness') and this row supplies its mechanism — the literal assertion is `callable(fn)`.
strengths.prevents_failure: a dangling ref or unregistered panel_id that dies in a RefUnresolved envelope on first live click
strengths.guard_population: the real live registries after a full composition boot — MEASURED by me: 1947 _REF_TABLE entries, 863 static custom_id bindings, 314 panels. Genuinely non-empty and genuinely the artifact. The weakness is the predicate, not the population.
strengths.successor_recommendation: Keep W1/W2 unchanged as the floor and add W7: every registered dispatch target must be reachable by >=1 executed acceptance case OR carry an expiring exemption row. Cost: this is the expensive one — it forces the corpus to grow toward the surface instead of the surface growing away from the corpus.

strengths.claim: superbot names its non-blocking checks 'advisory' in the CI step title itself (5 of 5 continue-on-error steps), so the string a human reads in the checks UI does not overclaim. superbot-next has zero continue-on-error steps and instead has checkers that print a real finding and exit 0 — which is strictly less honest, because the step name says nothing and the exit code says clean. On this one axis the older repo is the model.
strengths.quote: continue-on-error: true
strengths.contradicts: The estate framing that superbot is the debt-ridden repo and superbot-next the disciplined rebuild. On enforcement honesty the ranking inverts — this row agrees with R2-S06 and I re-state it because Challenge F's whole thesis is that a green tick is a claim, and a check that prints a defect while exiting 0 is a false claim with no label on it.
strengths.prevents_failure: a reviewer reading a green check as enforcement when the step is advisory
strengths.guard_population: the 5 continue-on-error steps in code-quality.yml. Not a guard over code; a naming convention over the gate list itself.
strengths.successor_recommendation: Make it mechanical rather than conventional: a meta-check that reds when any workflow step is continue-on-error without 'advisory' in its name, AND when any checker prints a finding while returning 0. Cost: ~40 lines, and the honesty it forces will make the board look worse before it looks better.

defects.area: THE CHEAT — acceptance coverage has no denominator over the bot
defects.claim: The acceptance oracle actuates 23 of 863 registered custom_id bindings (2.7%). MEASURED by me on two independent populations: a live composition boot gives _STATIC_TABLE = 863 (827 ComponentBinding + 36 NavBinding); a scan of all 533 goldens gives 86 click steps + 6 modal steps hitting 23 distinct custom_ids (475 command + 66 slash steps otherwise). No checker in either repo asserts a floor on that ratio — I grepped every tools/*.py and superbot's scripts/ for a coverage-ratio assertion and the only 'coverage' scripts are check_ci_coverage.py / check_codeql_coverage.py, which are about whether a workflow ran.
defects.contradicts: M11-S04/R5-S02 (the denominator assertion) and the estate's reading of '533 goldens green' as evidence the bot works. The denominator that IS asserted is goldens-replayed vs goldens-on-disk. The denominator that is NEVER asserted is goldens vs the 863-control surface. An implementer optimizing for green adds controls and never adds goldens: every gate stays green forever while the unproven surface grows without bound.
defects.failure_scenario: A user opens the Economy hub and clicks 'Transfer'. The button's custom_id is one of the 840 never actuated by any golden; its handler resolves to a callable (W1 green), its panel is registered (W2 green), its subsystem is `ported` with 8 goldens covering the `!balance` prefix command (parity gate green), and it declares no store/event so the A-16 depth floor is vacuous for it. The transfer silently does nothing — or debits without crediting — and all 7 required checks are green on the commit that shipped it.
defects.new_failure_class: unbounded unproven surface: the ratio of shipped controls to proven controls can only get worse, and no instrument reports it
defects.successor_recommendation: Publish the ratio as a first-class number in CI and ratchet it: proven_controls / registered_controls, with a committed floor that may only rise, and a per-control exemption row that expires (F-S05's shape). COST: this is the expensive strengthening — it forces either a much larger acceptance corpus or a much smaller surface, and it will make the true state visible on day one (about 2.7%), which is a political cost as much as an engineering one. It is also the ONLY strengthening that makes 'the bot works' a measured claim rather than an inference.

defects.area: THE EFFECT-GATE CHEAT — declaring an audit verb is not writing an audit row
defects.claim: The successor's flagship architectural claim (audit is a property of the mutation engine; 175 of 175 CompoundOpSpecs carry a non-empty audit_verb) is proven by observable EFFECT in 3 of 533 goldens (0.56%), all four kernel-band files, asserting exactly 1 distinct mutation_type corpus-wide: xp_awarded. MEASURED: 3 goldens carry an `audit_log` key in db_delta, 3 carry `event_outbox`, all under parity/goldens/kernel/; I dumped kernel_audited_prefix_command.json's audit_log.added and it is a single xp.award row. Every other golden has audit_log and event_outbox stripped from BOTH sides of the diff by the kernel-surface-drift disposition.
defects.quote:
dispositions = load_dispositions()
    out = copy.deepcopy(doc)
    kernel_band = doc.get("subsystem") == "kernel"
    drift = None if kernel_band else dispositions.get("kernel-surface-drift")
    if drift and drift.get("encoding") == "normalizer":
        _drop_kernel_surfaces(out, list(drift.get("tables") or []),
                              list(drift.get("events") or []))
defects.contradicts: M9-S03 ('Audit is a property of the mutation engine, not a call authors must remember. ONE call site … Measured live: 175 of 175 registered CompoundOpSpecs carry a non-empty audit_verb (100%)') read as proof the audit spine works. It proves 175 non-empty strings pass a compiler predicate. It does not prove 174 of them ever produce a row. Also contradicts R5-D10, which counted the strip's breadth but not how few documents survive it carrying an audit assertion — the true figure is 3.
defects.failure_scenario: An implementer refactors the workflow engine's audit write (a column rename, a txn-boundary move, an early return on a leg failure). Every CompoundOpSpec still declares its audit_verb, so manifest-validate is green; 530 of 533 goldens strip audit_log from both documents, so golden-parity is green; the 3 kernel goldens only exercise xp.award, which happens to still work. The bot ships and the moderator who later asks 'who deleted that channel?' gets an empty audit trail for 174 of 175 operations — the exact accountability guarantee the rebuild was for.
defects.new_failure_class: declaration-proven-not-effect-proven: a 100% compiler statistic standing in for a 0.6% effect statistic, with the same word ('audit coverage') used for both
defects.successor_recommendation: Assert the spine on every case (F-S06's inversion), and separately require one effect-asserting acceptance case per CompoundOpSpec before that op may be declared live — 175 cases, minted against the new bot, each asserting the audit row it claims to write. COST: 175 acceptance cases is weeks of work and it cannot be borrowed from the old bot's captures (the old bot has no such spine), so it must be authored fresh. That is precisely why it was skipped; it is also the only thing that makes the audit claim true.

defects.area: THE UNFLIP CHEAT — the 'one-way door' opens in a single PR
defects.claim: check_parity_depth's R4 rule is documented as the structural guard on the ported->pending direction ('this checker cannot see git history, so the ported->pending direction is guarded structurally'). It keys on a ratchet row existing while status is pending — so deleting the ratchet row in the SAME commit that sets the status defeats it. MEASURED in-process against the real checker: baseline cpd.check() -> 0 problems; then karma set to 'pending', depth.ratchet['karma'] popped, and its 8 goldens truncated to 1 in the docs map -> cpd.check() -> 0 problems. Script EXIT=0. run_golden_parity --gate then skips karma entirely: 'PENDING (expected-red, reported not failing)'.
defects.quote:
if row is None:
            continue
        covered = covered_surfaces(docs_by_subsystem.get(subsystem, []))
        for dim in ("events", "tables", "settings"):
            committed = row.get(dim, 0)
            current = len(covered[dim])
            if isinstance(committed, int) and current < committed:
                problems.append(
                    f"R3 {subsystem}: covered {dim} count fell {committed} -> "
                    f"{current} (the ratchet is one-way)")
        # R4 — a ratchet row on a pending subsystem = a reverted flip
        if status == "pending":
            problems.append(
                f"R4 {subsystem}: has a depth.ratchet row but status is "
                f"pending — ported is a one-way door (design-spec §6 gate 5)")
defects.contradicts: M11-S07/R5-S08 and the checker's own docstring, which present R3/R4 as a one-way door and a one-way ratchet. Both fences are keyed on the SAME row an author may delete, and neither the checker nor any test compares against git history. The 'one-way door' is a door with the hinge on the inside.
defects.failure_scenario: A release is blocked because 3 karma goldens went red after a refactor. The implementer, optimizing for green and not for deception, edits parity.yml: karma status ported -> pending, removes the karma ratchet row, and writes 'temporarily unflipped pending the karma rework' in the PR body. All 7 required checks go green, karma's 8 goldens stop being replayed by anything, and the temporary unflip is never noticed again because no gate reports the ported count falling. Users hit the broken karma path in production with a fully green pipeline behind it.
defects.new_failure_class: self-service scope reduction: the gate's coverage set is editable by the same PR the gate is judging
defects.successor_recommendation: Move the ported roster out of the checked-in file the PR can edit, or (cheaper and sufficient) commit a monotonic `ported_count` in a separate CODEOWNERS-fenced file and red when the live count is below it; better still, have CI compare parity.yml against the merge-base copy so any ported->pending transition is an explicit, labelled, reviewable event. COST: one extra file and a git-fetch in CI (~10 lines); the real cost is that unflipping becomes a visible decision instead of a maintenance edit.

defects.area: THE REAL-GUILD CHEAT — a signed fact is an unvalidated string
defects.claim: The V-5 live-verification registry accepts a fully forged sign-off. MEASURED: I constructed a record with surface_id='/NO_SUCH_COMMAND_AT_ALL', signer='me', signed_at='not-a-date', build_sha='zzzz' and two evidence rows with links 'x' and 'y', and validate_record returned [] (zero problems), EXIT=0. Nothing resolves an evidence link, checks the SHA against the PR head, checks the timestamp is a date, or checks that surface_id names a registered command/panel/custom_id. And check_verified_live's V3 only requires >=1 record for a subsystem MARKED verified — there is no per-surface coverage floor, so one forged record per subsystem flips all 50 dashboard rows to verified.
defects.contradicts: The module docstring at lines 15-17: 'A VERIFIED record is a signed fact: signer, timestamp, build SHA, and at least one evidence row are mandatory.' Measured: all four are mandatory as NON-EMPTY STRINGS and none is validated as a fact. Also sharpens M11-D01/R5-D07/R6-D02, which established the registry is EMPTY (0 records) — the deeper finding is that filling it costs nothing, so 'empty' and 'full' would carry the same evidentiary weight.
defects.failure_scenario: At cutover the owner asks 'is the new bot verified against a real guild?' A session under deadline appends 50 records — one per subsystem, each with plausible scenario_steps, a signer string, today's date, the current SHA and two evidence links pointing at transcript paths that were never written — runs check_verified_live (EXIT=0, '50 subsystems (50 verified)'), and the dashboard reads fully verified. The owner swaps the production token on the strength of a document that no machine and no human ever checked, and finds out in the live guild.
defects.new_failure_class: self-attested evidence: the highest-authority tier in the estate is the one with the weakest validation, so the strongest-sounding claim is the cheapest to make
defects.successor_recommendation: Make the record derive from an artifact the author cannot type: require build_sha to equal the PR head SHA (CI can check this), require each evidence link to resolve to a file in the repo or a fetchable URL that CI HEADs, require surface_id to be present in manifest.snapshot.json's command/panel/custom_id projections, and add a coverage floor (N records per ported subsystem, ratcheted). COST: the link-resolution leg needs network in CI and will be flaky; the surface_id and SHA legs are free and close most of the hole. Do the free legs first — they turn 'a string someone typed' into 'a claim about a real surface at a real build'.

defects.area: THE RE-BLESS CHEAT — eight committed buttons that regenerate the artifacts the gates compare against
defects.claim: 8 of the repo's tools ship a self-blessing regeneration flag (check_compat_frozen --write, manifest_compile --write, mint_golden --write, plugin_pin --write, check_lockfile_fresh --regen, check_escape_hatches --tighten, check_parity_depth --write-ratchet, check_sim_gate --write-baseline), covering 5 of the 7 required contexts. check_compat_frozen --write is unconditional: it derives the pin from manifest.snapshot.json and overwrites the file, returning 0 without comparing anything. Its stated control is CODEOWNERS review, and .github/CODEOWNERS is the blanket line `* @menno420` — i.e. the same review every file gets.
defects.quote:
current = derive()
    if args.write:
        PIN.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        PIN.write_text(json.dumps(current, indent=1, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
        print(f"check_compat_frozen: pin written -> {PIN}")
        return 0
defects.contradicts: R5-S05 and M8-S02, which read the compat pin (413 command rows, 265 legacy custom_ids) and the boot-gate recompile as hard contract enforcement. The chain is source -> snapshot -> pin, and every link has a --write. These gates detect FORGETTING to regenerate; they cannot detect a wrong change, because the wrong change regenerates cleanly. The only real control is one human reading a 413-row JSON diff.
defects.failure_scenario: An implementer renames a command's dispatch key while refactoring (say `economy.balance` -> `economy.bal`). check_compat_frozen reds. They run the command the error message itself tells them to run — 'amend the pin (--write) in this PR' — and the pin now blesses the rename. manifest-validate reds next; they run manifest_compile --write. Both gates go green in under a minute. Every existing persistent panel in every guild still carries the OLD custom_id baked into its message; those buttons now resolve to nothing, and the contract layer that existed precisely to catch this signed off on it.
defects.new_failure_class: regeneration-as-approval: the remediation instruction printed by the failing gate is the exact command that defeats it
defects.successor_recommendation: Three graded fixes. (a) Free: every --write must print a human-readable DIFF of what it is about to bless and require an explicit `--i-reviewed` flag; a bare --write refuses. (b) Cheap: CODEOWNERS must fence the pinned artifacts to a distinct reviewer path so a pin change is a visibly different review from a code change — today the blanket `* @menno420` makes it indistinguishable. (c) Structural: for the compat pin specifically, red on any REMOVAL or RENAME regardless of regeneration (additions are free, deletions need a ledger entry), which is the one-way-ratchet shape F-S04 already proves the repo knows how to build. COST: (a) and (b) are an afternoon; (c) forces a deprecation discipline the repo does not have yet.

defects.area: THE ESCAPE-HATCH CHEAT — the ratchet counts the hatch nobody uses
defects.claim: The escape-hatch ratchet — 'required CI from the first kernel PR through post-cutover, NO EXPIRY' — counts three markers, and I counted all three in the 2.27 MB manifest.snapshot.json: '"view:' = 0, '"tier": 3' = 0, 'escape_hatch' = 0. Meanwhile sb/spec/panels.py:362 labels renderer_override '[S] escape hatch (§2.9)' in its own comment, and 218 panel nodes in the same snapshot carry one (315 raw text occurrences). So 69% of panels take the escape hatch that has no ratchet, and the ratchet with NO EXPIRY guards a population of zero.
defects.quote:
is_tier3 = (isinstance(ref, str) and ref.startswith("view:")) or \
                node.get("tier") == 3 or bool(node.get("escape_hatch"))
defects.contradicts: M8-S04 ('The escape-hatch ratchet is at a GENUINE zero and the counter demonstrably fires') — which is true and is the trap. The counter fires on an injected tier-3 node; no author will ever write one, because renderer_override is the ergonomic, blessed, uncounted path to the same freedom. A guard that fires on injected positives but never on real authoring behaviour is the most convincing kind of vacuous guard, because it passes the negative-control test.
defects.failure_scenario: A subsystem is ported under deadline. Rather than expressing its panel in the grammar, the author writes `renderer_override=HandlerRef('x.render')` with a one-line justification ('the shipped embed is live-data-parameterized') and hand-builds the embed and components in Python. manifest-validate is green (tier-3 count still 0, baseline still {} / 0), the panel renders, and the kernel's framework-injected navigation never runs for it — which is exactly the measured state today: 150 of 314 panels render zero engine-injected nav. Two years on, the 'one kernel runtime interprets every panel' architecture is a minority code path and the ratchet that was supposed to prevent that reports a permanent, honest zero.
defects.new_failure_class: ratchet aimed at the wrong marker: an escape hatch with a cost and an escape hatch without one, and the authors take the free one 218 times
defects.successor_recommendation: Point the existing (well-built, one-way, F-S04) counter at renderer_override and legacy_view — the markers real authors use — and stamp today's 218 as the baseline that may only fall. The justification requirement already exists at sb/kernel/panels/compile.py:130-134 and the 181 distinct justification strings show authors do write real ones, so the culture is there; only the counter is aimed wrong. COST: essentially free to implement (one predicate change), and it immediately converts a 0-of-0 green into a 218 debt number the owner has to look at. That visibility is the whole point and the whole cost.

defects.area: THE UNIT-TIER CHEAT — tests that assert source TEXT, over code no test executes
defects.claim: The required code-quality gate is `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q` with only pytest+pyyaml installed. Inside it, 9 assertions across 3 test files (tests/unit/app/test_main_wiring.py, tests/unit/band4/test_band4_community.py, tests/unit/workflow/test_spec_and_fences.py — counted by grep) assert on inspect.getsource() substrings, including exact whitespace continuations, over sb/app/main.py's run_app — the 624-line composition root that no test ever executes.
defects.quote:
src = inspect.getsource(app_main.run_app)
        assert "test_guild_id = moderation_test_guild(cfg)" in src
        assert "if test_guild_id is not None:" in src
        assert ("DiscordModerationActions(bot, allowed_guild_id=test_guild_id)"
                in src)
defects.contradicts: M11-S08 and the estate's use of '3,648 green tests' as evidence. M8-D03 established run_app is never executed; this row supplies the mechanism by which it is nonetheless 'tested'. An implementer optimizing for green satisfies these by writing the right TEXT — the assertion is literally string containment — and a semantically equivalent refactor (renaming the local, reflowing the call across lines) reds the suite while changing no behaviour, which trains the team to treat these tests as formatting rules.
defects.failure_scenario: During a boot-order fix the author moves the moderation-actions install above the test-guild gate but keeps the source lines the assertions match (they are checked with `src.index(needle) > gate_at`, so a reorder is caught — but only for those 4 needles among 18 boot steps). For any of the other 14 steps, reordering, deleting or no-op-ing the call leaves all 9 text assertions green. The bot boots in production with a step silently skipped, and 3,648 tests plus the required code-quality gate report clean.
defects.new_failure_class: text-equality standing in for execution: the composition root is the highest-risk 624 lines in the repo and it is verified by grepping itself
defects.successor_recommendation: Execute run_app under a fake-adapter profile and assert the ORDER of observed install calls (a recorder object collecting call names), replacing all 9 source-text assertions with one execution trace compared to a committed ordered list. sb/app/verify_boot.py already proves a side-effect-free boot profile is buildable — the fix is to make verify_boot run main.run_app rather than re-implement 3 of its 18 steps (M8-D02). COST: real work — the adapters need fakes for every port — but it collapses two existing defects (unexecuted root, parallel re-implementation) into one mechanism, and it is the thing that makes 'the bot boots' a tested claim.

defects.area: THE COG-PORTABILITY CHEAT — the one gate behind the owner's hard requirement returns [] when its population is absent
defects.claim: plugin_boot_problems — the only automated proof of the owner's stated cog-portability requirement — returns an empty problem list, verbatim commented 'nothing to prove', when no exemplar is present in the checkout. The exemplars are in-tree files under examples/; nothing outside this function asserts they exist, and check_runtime_smoke exits 0 either way.
defects.quote:
if not entry_points:
        return []  # no exemplars in this checkout — nothing to prove
defects.contradicts: M11-S03 ('The owner's cog-portability requirement is the ONE product property with a real gate behind it') and R3-S8. The gate is real when the exemplars are there and silently absent when they are not — and M8-D04 measured the degradation directly (`mv examples /tmp` -> EXIT=0). Compounding it: R3-D5 measured that 29 of the 49 in-tree manifests could not be shipped as plugins under this contract anyway, so the 2 exemplars that ARE proven are the easy shape, not the shape the owner asked about.
defects.failure_scenario: An examples/ cleanup (or a packaging change that stops shipping examples/ in the CI checkout) removes the exemplars. Every gate stays green. Months later the owner tries the thing he asked for on 2026-08-23 — take an existing cog and slot it in — and discovers the plugin path has drifted (a facet grew, the lock format changed) with no red build anywhere in between, because the only test of it had been proving nothing since the cleanup.
defects.new_failure_class: population-optional guard on the single owner-named product requirement — the highest-value gate is the one that can quietly become a no-op
defects.successor_recommendation: Assert the population, not just the result: `assert len(entry_points) >= 2` with the expected keys, so a missing exemplar reds. This is F-S02's tripwire applied to the one place the owner would most notice its absence. COST: two lines. Then the larger fix: add a THIRD exemplar shaped like a real ported cog (one declaring `stores`), because the current two prove only the facet-free easy case that R3-D5 shows 29 of 49 real subsystems do not fit.

defects.area: THE PRESENTATION CHEAT — no required gate ever renders a Discord message
defects.claim: install_panel_runtime returns BEFORE installing the presenter when discord is not importable, and the required code-quality job installs only `pytest pyyaml` (named-gates.yml:52). MEASURED: the 4 DiscordPanelPresenter tests skip in that environment — `python3 -m pytest tests/unit/app/test_cut1_surfaces.py -q -p no:randomly` -> '19 passed, 4 skipped', EXIT=0. So every green required check runs against a bot whose entire RenderedPanel -> Discord message layer is absent, and R5-D01 already established that the parity harness substitutes its OWN serializer (rendered_panel_payload, imported by nothing but parity) on the acceptance side.
defects.quote:
if importlib.util.find_spec("discord") is None:
        logger.info("discord not importable — panel presenter left uninstalled")
        return
    from sb.adapters.discord.panel_view import DiscordPanelPresenter

    panel_engine.install_panel_presenter(DiscordPanelPresenter())
defects.contradicts: M9-S06/M11-S08 celebrate 'the entire panel registry boots and renders all 314 panels with NEITHER discord.py NOR asyncpg installed' as proof of port isolation. It IS good isolation and it is exactly why no required gate exercises the real presenter: the property that makes the kernel testable is the property that makes the last mile untested. The strength and the defect are the same design decision, and no lane said so in one sentence.
defects.failure_scenario: A change to build_embed or build_files in sb/adapters/discord/panel_view.py (a field-length overflow past Discord's 1024-char embed field limit, a components-per-row miscount, a None where discord.py wants a str) ships. code-quality green (presenter never constructed, its 4 tests skipped), manifest-validate green (headless boot, presenter deliberately uninstalled), architecture green (AST scans), golden-parity green if it runs at all (parity uses its own serializer, not this class). In the live guild every panel in the affected shape throws HTTPException on send and the user sees nothing at all.
defects.new_failure_class: the last mile is the only unproven mile: 863 bindings and 314 panels are proven up to the point where bytes meet the platform, and no further
defects.successor_recommendation: Add one required job with discord.py installed (no token, no network) that constructs DiscordPanelPresenter and renders all 314 panels into real discord.Embed/View objects, asserting only that construction succeeds and each object satisfies discord.py's own limits. That is a genuine capability floor and it is cheap. COST: one CI job with the pinned lock (~2 min) and the discipline of keeping the presenter constructible headlessly — which the code already nearly supports.

defects.area: THE STRUCTURAL-GATE CHEAT — six absence assertions that a bot doing nothing passes perfectly
defects.claim: The required `architecture` context is six AST scans, and I ran all six bare: check_symbol_shadowing, check_no_skip, check_config_usage, check_metric_cardinality, check_egress, check_money_race — all EXIT=0. Every one asserts the ABSENCE of something (a shadowed symbol, a discord import outside adapters, an os.getenv outside kernel/config, an unbounded metric label, an unfenced egress call, an unfenced money mutation). None asserts the PRESENCE of a capability. An empty sb/domain would pass all six with a perfect score, and check_money_race would report '0 violations' most confidently of all.
defects.quote:
- name: Symbol shadowing
        run: python3 tools/check_symbol_shadowing.py
      - name: Adapter no-skip fence
        run: python3 tools/check_no_skip.py
      - name: Config-accessor seam
        run: python3 tools/check_config_usage.py
      - name: Metric cardinality
        run: python3 tools/check_metric_cardinality.py
      - name: Egress fence (RC-21/A-5)
        run: python3 tools/check_egress.py
      - name: Money-race lint (F-001/F-002 class)
        run: python3 tools/check_money_race.py
defects.contradicts: M8-S01/S03/S06, M10-S1, R6-S02 — all of which are correct that these fences fire on injected positives and are genuinely stricter than superbot's equivalents. The contradiction is with how the estate READS a green architecture check: as evidence the architecture is sound. It is evidence that no forbidden pattern is present, which is a strictly weaker claim and is maximally satisfied by code that does nothing. M8-D09 already showed one of them (check_no_skip) is bypassed by importlib.import_module, i.e. even the absence claim is name-based.
defects.failure_scenario: A subsystem is delivered as 40 panels with 200 controls, every handler a resolvable coroutine that returns a Reply with a placeholder embed and touches no store. All six architecture checks pass (no forbidden imports because there are no imports; no money races because no money moves; no unbounded metrics because no metrics). check_runtime_smoke passes (every ref callable, every panel registered). The subsystem is declared `ported` with 4 goldens of its `!help`-shaped commands. Nobody notices for a release cycle that it does nothing, because every instrument the team trusts is an absence instrument.
defects.new_failure_class: absence-only enforcement: an estate of 77 executable guards in which zero assert that a capability EXISTS, so quality is measured entirely by what is missing
defects.successor_recommendation: Add exactly one presence gate and make it required — the F-D01 ratio (proven controls / registered controls) with a floor — and keep all six absence fences unchanged. The insight to carry into the rebuild is architectural, not procedural: absence guards are cheap, composable and should be many; presence guards are expensive and should be ONE, but there must be one, or the whole apparatus is silent on the only question that matters. COST: see F-D01.

defects.area: THE BOOT-GATE CHEAT — the pre-connect refusal compares an artifact against its own generator
defects.claim: Boot-gate leg A recompiles the manifest in-process and refuses to start on divergence from the committed manifest.snapshot.json — and manifest_compile.py ships --write, which regenerates that exact file from the same source. So the gate's assertion is 'the committed artifact equals what this source produces', which is true by construction after one command. It detects forgetting to recompile; it cannot detect a wrong manifest, because a wrong manifest recompiles to itself.
defects.quote: def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
defects.contradicts: M8-S02, M9-S04 and R4-S09, which present leg A as 'a hard pre-connect refusal' and 'FAILED_STARTUP, not a warning' — all true and all about the wrong axis. R3-D12 half-saw this ('the gain is partly repaid at the snapshot') but framed it as an authoring cost rather than as a limit on what the gate can prove. Every 'DRIFT' the digest cites as evidence of strength (M8-S02's changed description string) is a forgot-to-recompile detection, which is the only class this design can catch.
defects.failure_scenario: An author deletes a panel's action list while refactoring (or a compile predicate silently stops matching — F-D02's class). They run manifest_compile.py --write and commit. Leg A is green at merge and green at production boot; check_namespace validates the same regenerated snapshot (M8-D10 measured it green over a stale artifact for the inverse reason); check_compat_frozen --write blesses the derived pin. The bot starts cleanly with a panel that has lost its controls, and the gate whose entire purpose is 'refuse to boot on manifest divergence' has nothing to diverge from.
defects.new_failure_class: self-consistency mistaken for correctness — the strongest-sounding gate in the repo (FAILED_STARTUP before the gateway) is a checksum of source against itself
defects.successor_recommendation: Keep leg A (forgot-to-recompile is a real class worth catching) and stop describing it as a correctness gate in the docs and session cards, because that description is what stops anyone building the gate that would catch a wrong manifest. Then add the cheap independent oracle: red when the recompile REMOVES a declared command, panel, action or store that the previous snapshot had, unless a ledger row names the removal. COST: near zero (a set-difference against the merge-base snapshot); the value is that it converts every deletion from an invisible regeneration into a stated decision.

defects.area: THE NO-OP HANDLER CHEAT — the estate ships a blessed primitive for a control that does nothing, and nothing counts it
defects.claim: pending_handler() registers a handler that returns Reply(BLOCKED, message) and nothing else. Such a ref satisfies check_runtime_smoke W1 (it is callable), W2 (its panel is registered), check_orphan_pendings O1 (it has a _REF_TABLE entry) and O2 (it is referenced by a registered panel) by construction. MEASURED at this pin: 4 of 1947 registered refs are pending terminals — so the practice is small today. What is measured and damning is that NO gate distinguishes 4 from 1947: I found no count, ratchet, baseline or test anywhere that bounds them, and check_orphan_pendings' baseline is explicitly the opposite direction (it reds only on pendings that are UNREACHABLE).
defects.quote:
O2 orphan — a REGISTERED handler whose name ends ``_pending`` that is
     referenced by NO registered panel and NO manifest ref: the exact #412
     class (registered but unreachable — dead declared surface that rots
     into confusion). RED against ``_KNOWN_ORPHANS``, the burn-down
     baseline captured at this checker's landing
defects.contradicts: M9-S05 and R3-S5 present check_orphan_pendings as the model guard that runs over the REAL population (936 handler refs walked, EXIT=0) — correct, and it is aimed at the opposite failure. It guarantees a pending handler is REACHABLE. A control that is reachable and refuses is exactly the shape of the useless-but-green bot, and the guard that walks the real population is the one certifying it. Also sharpens R6-D06's 'guards prove registration, never usefulness' by naming the in-repo primitive that makes the gap trivially exploitable.
defects.failure_scenario: A port band ships under deadline: 40 panels, 200 controls, 180 of them wired to pending_handler with honest 'not armed yet' copy. Every gate is green — W1/W2 pass (callable, registered), O1/O2 pass (reachable, not orphan), the architecture fences pass (no writes, so no money races and no unfenced SQL), and the subsystem is flipped `ported` with goldens of its read-only commands. The owner opens the bot, clicks eleven things in a row and every one says 'not available yet', while the dashboard, the checks and the session card all read complete. That is the useless-but-green bot in its purest form and it requires no dishonesty at any step.
defects.new_failure_class: honest-refusal-at-scale: the shape is individually virtuous (a stated refusal beats a dead button) and collectively indistinguishable from a finished product to every instrument in the estate
defects.successor_recommendation: Bound it and surface it: a committed per-subsystem pending count that may only fall (F-S04's one-way shape), the total printed in the boot summary and in the operator help card, and a rule that a subsystem may not be flipped `ported` while more than N% of its declared controls are pending terminals. COST: one baseline file and one predicate. This is the cheapest of all twelve strengthenings and it closes the single cheat that requires zero bad faith to execute — which makes it the one an implementer optimizing for green is most likely to reach for.

honest_nulls: I did NOT execute the golden-parity replay, so every claim about what the oracle PROVES is derived from the golden documents and the driver source, not from a run. `tools/run_golden_parity.py --gate` cannot bind here (no asyncpg, no Postgres) — I did not spend budget re-confirming the binding failure the digest already measured.

I did NOT actually mutate parity.yml on disk for F-D03. The cheat was executed IN-PROCESS against the real checker's own check() function with deep-copied inputs (baseline 0 problems -> cheat 0 problems). What I did not test is whether some OTHER gate — a test under tests/unit/, a CODEOWNERS path rule, or a workflow step I did not read — would independently notice a ported->pending transition. I grepped no further; treat 'no other gate notices' as unverified, and the checker-level result as measured.

I did NOT verify that the 23 clicked custom_ids map onto 23 of the 863 static bindings. 7 of them are run-minted session ids per the digest (M11-D04), and I did not resolve the remaining 16 against _STATIC_TABLE. So '23 of 863' is an upper bound on actuation; the true figure is 16-23 of 863. I state the ratio as 2.7% because that is the generous reading — the honest range is 1.9-2.7%.

I did NOT measure how many of the 1947 registered refs are reachable from a user surface at all. 863 are custom_id-bound; the other ~1084 include command handlers, providers and internal refs. The 'a tree of 1947 no-op coroutines' framing in F-S08 is rhetorical about scale, not a claim that 1947 controls exist.

F-D09's claim that the presenter layer is untested by any REQUIRED gate rests on named-gates.yml's job/install mapping, which I read, plus a measured local skip. I did NOT confirm which workflow job GitHub's required context `code-quality` actually resolves to — both named-gates.yml and ci.yml define jobs, and M11-D10 measured that none of these workflows has run on main since 2026-07-17 while the pin advanced 100 commits. If the required context binds to a job I did not read, the install list may differ.

I did NOT test the superbot side of any cheat by execution. superbot's pytest suite does not collect here (discord.py absent; prior lanes recorded EXIT=1 with hundreds of collection errors) and I chose not to build stubs — my two superbot rows (F-S02, F-S09) are source reads, and F-S09 restates R2-S06 rather than adding measurement. A full Challenge-F pass on superbot's 45 checkers is NOT in this lane.

I could NOT construct the strongest form of the challenge — actually building the green-but-useless subsystem — because writing into either clone was forbidden and copying the 85 MB tree to scratch was not a good use of the budget. Every cheat above is either measured in-process against the real checker (F-D03, F-D04), measured over the real artifacts (F-D01, F-D02, F-D06, F-D07, F-D12), or read verbatim from the source that implements the degradation (F-D08, F-D09, F-D11). None is a constructed end-to-end demonstration, and a planner should read them as 'the gate cannot distinguish X from Y', never as 'X was shipped'.

I did NOT price any of the strengthenings in real hours. Every COST line is a shape judgement (free / afternoon / weeks / political), not an estimate, and F-D01's and F-D02's costs in particular are the kind that get revised upward once someone starts.

REFUTED MY OWN EXPECTATION, recorded because it was the sharpest thing I went looking for: I expected the 218 renderer_override justifications to be boilerplate, which would have made F-D06 a much stronger row. Measured: 218 uses carry 181 DISTINCT justification strings, several of them specific and technically substantive ('the shipped step card is flow-state-parameterized end to end'). The authors are not gaming the justification requirement; they are using an escape hatch that costs a sentence when the alternative costs a redesign. That is a much more sympathetic — and much harder to fix — failure than the one I was hunting.

I did NOT examine spider-bot at all. Its guards genuinely walk real production objects (M12), and a Challenge-F pass on the small live bot would be the natural control case for whether these cheats are a scale artifact or a design artifact. That test was not run.

I dropped no verified row for space; the 12/12 caps were not binding. Two candidates were dropped as code smells rather than concrete failures per the survival rule: (a) check_metric_cardinality reporting '51 families' clean tells you nothing about whether any metric is ever read, and (b) the 44 skipped tests in the required code-quality run are only 25 accounted for (integration 14 + e2e 11), with ~19 unit skips I did not characterise and which could hide more of F-D09's class.

synthesis:
# The Successor Product Definition & Product Disposition Matrix

*Synthesis lane. Every claim below is either (a) an evidence id from the fleet digest, (b) a measurement I took myself this session against the frozen clones (marked **[mine]**), or (c) explicitly flagged as inference or OWNER_DECISION. Rows the adversarial pass REFUTED are not built on; where a refuted row has a salvageable corrected form I cite it as "(corrected)".*

---

## Part 0 — What the evidence actually settles, before any product opinion

Three facts frame everything, and two of them invert the estate's working assumption.

**Fact 1 — superbot's problem is not its runtime.** The removable mass is 43,121 of 243,961 lines (17.7%), and it is three named things, none of them architecture: BTD6 content (36,410 LOC path-wide, 14.9% of the runtime), ux_lab (4,937 LOC of an admin-only gallery that its own docstring says never writes), and readiness_repair.py (462 lines, zero production importers) — A-D02, A-D07, M3-D6, M3-D7. Meanwhile the doc corpus is 863 files / 185,658 lines, 76% the size of the runtime, with 176 files / 39,605 lines already machine-badged `historical`/`archive` and never harvested (A-D04, A-D05, A-S06). **The "too much history, too many trials and errors" is largely a documentation and content condition wearing an architecture costume.** That does not make the rebuild wrong — it changes what the rebuild is *for*.

**Fact 2 — superbot-next is a port, not a convergence, and it is a port of the invocation surface too.** 54 domain files matched above 0.55 similarity, 8 pairs ≥0.90, one byte-identical (R6-S09, corrected). And the surface came with it: of 413 compiled commands, **386 are prefix-only, 18 slash, 9 both — 27 of 413 (6.5%) reachable without the message_content privileged intent** (C-D01, D-D08, **[mine]** re-derived from `manifest.snapshot.json`). The required CI check `check_compat_frozen` freezes those 413 prefix names and 135 aliases; the two gates that would govern the *modern* surface (`check_slash_cap`, `check_intent_survival`) are non-required and run over 18 and 4 commands respectively (C-D03, C-D04, C-S04-refuted). **The ground-up rebuild made the 2020-era invocation vocabulary the one contract a merge cannot break.**

**Fact 3 — the acceptance oracle is a bot the owner has rejected.** `parity/README.md:20`: "The current bot is the oracle." The owner said on 2026-08-28 that the current build "is nothing like the desired product." Byte-parity to that oracle then *caused* fabricated behaviour: 28 frozen operator diagnostic cards shipped as 33 live commands including a `!check_database` that always reports "103/103 migrations" against 57 real migration files (R1-D1, R1-D3); a `!coglist` that lists 58 of the *old* bot's discord.py module names (M11-D05, R1-D7); a Server Management health badge frozen at the capture guild's permission answers (R1-D6); and 128 of 2,102 pinned user-facing strings carrying internal jargon that cannot now be improved without reddening a required check (D-D07). **C-D11 is the load-bearing product finding of the whole fleet: the successor's definition of "correct" was "identical to the thing being replaced."**

And one measurement I took that the fleet did not: **superbot-next's live message feed arms 2 of superbot's 9+ passive message stages** — the XP chat award and the four_twenty easter egg. Counting, chain, automod, image moderation, cleanup, the RPS tournament stage, the AI correction stage and the NL shell are all documented DORMANT ("their live feeds are named successors", `sb/adapters/discord/message_feed.py:1-33`) **[mine]**. Yet `automod` still declares 15 settings and `image_moderation` 8 (**[mine]**, per-subsystem census). **An operator of superbot-next today can toggle 23 safety settings that cannot change any behaviour, with nothing telling them so.** That, together with D-D04 (welcome is ON by default and structurally cannot fire) and D-D01 (an unrecognised command produces total silence), is the successor's actual product state.

---

## Part 1 — The Successor Product Definition

### 1.1 Who uses it, and what kinds of servers

**Evidenced, not assumed.** The content mix is the strongest signal available: BTD6 tower-defense assistance is the single largest capability at 74 of 413 commands (17.9%), Project Moon/Limbus Company is a second knowledge vertical, there are 11 game subsystems, a coin economy with mining/fishing/farming/creatures, a 🍃 420 easter egg, and `!fact / !joke / !quote / !trivia / !8ball` (**[mine]**, per-subsystem census; D-D11). Against that sits a very heavy operator surface: 42 diagnostic commands, a Server Management hub, a settings hub with 127 declared settings, and a 40-panel setup wizard (**[mine]**). There is no billing surface, no tenancy model, no rate-limit budget per guild, and no shard configuration anywhere in either tree.

So the honest reading is: **a bot for a small number of gaming-community Discord servers that the owner and people he knows run, where the owner is also the operator.** Three user roles, in descending population:

- **The member.** Wants to play the games, earn coins, ask the BTD6 assistant a question, level up, get a role, and never think about the bot. Types one thing and expects one answer.
- **The server owner / staff.** Sets the bot up once, wants moderation and logging to work without study, and comes back rarely — to change a channel binding, check a warning history, or turn something off.
- **The platform operator (today: the owner alone).** Needs to know at 2am *what this process is doing, what it refused, and who changed what* — and to fix it without a redeploy.

**OWNER_DECISION — is this ever a public, multi-tenant product?** The evidence cannot settle it: multi-guild plumbing is real (per-guild bindings, `on_guild_join` onboarding, guild teardown), but nothing is sized for it. **Recommended default: no.** Design for small-N, owner-operated servers; keep multi-guild *correctness* (no cross-guild leakage, clean teardown) because it is cheap and both bots already have it, but do not pay for multi-tenant *scale* (sharding, per-guild quotas, a dashboard, onboarding funnels). If the answer is ever yes, the cost is concentrated in exactly two places — the operator diagnostics surface and the setup journey — and both are being rebuilt anyway.

### 1.2 The primary interaction model

**One grouped slash tree is the invocation surface. Prefix commands survive as a compatibility layer for the owner's own muscle memory, not as the product.**

This is the single highest-leverage decision, and it is decided by arithmetic rather than taste. Discord's caps are already encoded as executable constants in superbot-next — `SLASH_CAP_TOP_LEVEL = 100`, `SLASH_CAP_PER_GROUP = 25`, one level of nesting (C-S03, `sb/spec/governance.py:45-46`). With 49 subsystems, one top-level command per subsystem uses 49 of 100 slots. Only three subsystems exceed 25 commands and need splitting: btd6 (74), diagnostic (42), mining (37) **[mine]**. **The whole 413-command surface fits the platform's own cap with room to double.** Nobody had to discover this: superbot's own 2026-07-03 analysis measured it and recommended it, five days before superbot-next's first commit, and superbot then *shipped it once* — `cogs/btd6/_unified.py` collapses five prefix groups into a single `/btd6` tree, explicitly budgeted against the caps (C-S05, C-D02). The rebuild did not generalise it.

Why this matters as *product*, not plumbing:
- **Discoverability.** Slash gives the member a typed, auto-completing, permission-filtered list. Neither bot uses autocomplete at all — the token appears once in superbot as a comment and twice in superbot-next as "dormant successor" (C-D07) — while superbot carries 991 LOC of pagination machinery to work around not having it.
- **Survivability.** message_content is a privileged intent Discord can deny. Today that denial darks 386 of 413 commands, and superbot-next's own written justification for degrading rather than refusing to boot ("every slash command still serves") is false at this pin by a factor of 15 (C-D01, R4-D01).
- **Privacy.** 13 of the 14 commands that declare an ephemeral reply are slash-only, and global slash sync is hardcoded off (`main.py:616`), so the entire declared-private surface of the bot is currently unreachable (D-D03).

**Panels stay, but subordinate.** A panel is what you get *after* an invocation, for a task with state — configuring something, browsing an inventory, walking a wizard. It is not a substitute for a command. Two measurements set the ceiling: 153 of 314 panels declare zero actions (49%, settled), and across the entire 534-golden corpus only 23 of 863 registered component bindings are ever actuated (2.7%) (F-D01, R5-D03). **The successor ships panels only where there is state to manipulate; a panel with no actions is a message, and should be sent as one.**

### 1.3 What the operator experience should feel like

**It should feel like the bot is telling you the truth about itself, unprompted.** Four concrete properties, each traceable to a defect this fleet measured:

1. **It always answers.** superbot answers every failed command from one global handler with a 7-branch ladder including a typo suggestion (D-S01). superbot-next answers *nothing* — `prefix_typo_reply` returns `None` on both miss branches, so `!helpp` and `!seting` produce total silence (D-D01). The successor's rule: **there is no silent path.** Every invocation produces exactly one of {the result, a stated refusal with a reason, a suggestion, an honest "that isn't a thing"}.

2. **Nothing renders a number it did not just read.** This is the anti-`!check_database` rule. 12 files in superbot-next freeze the old bot's self-description as constants and ship them as live-looking output, and only 4 carry the formal label (R1-D8). The counter-example already exists in the same subsystem, same PR: `process_state.py` does real `/proc` reads and degrades to `"n/a"` rather than inventing a figure (R1-S2, corrected). **A surface describing the bot's own state must vary with that state, and the successor ships a test that asserts exactly that** (R1-D12 names it; nobody has written it).

3. **A control you can see is a control that works.** 15 automod settings and 8 image-moderation settings are renderable today while their engines are unarmed **[mine]**; the welcome greeting is on by default and cannot fire (D-D04); the Cog Manager's Load/Unload/Reload buttons are wired to a handler that says the capability does not exist while its select and pagination stay live, so the surface *looks* functional (R3-D8). The successor's rule: **a setting whose consumer is not armed is not rendered** — and where a surface must exist before its engine does, it uses the `pending_handler` primitive, which returns a stated refusal instead of a spinner (F-S07, corrected: 13 live call sites, 9 of them in ux_lab).

4. **You can fix it from inside Discord.** superbot has two independent in-Discord recovery levers for a misbehaving cog, with a deliberate and documented protection asymmetry (R4-S06, R3-S2). superbot-next has zero — `reload_extension` appears nowhere under `sb/`, and the only lever is a process restart (R4-D10). At 2am, on a phone, "restart everything" is not a recovery tool. Likewise: superbot mirrors Discord's own audit log into the log channel so an operator can answer *who changed this* (D-S09); superbot-next writes one `audit_log` row inside the transaction for all 175 of its compound ops — its central architectural claim — **and provides no way to read them from Discord at all** (D-D09, M9-S03).

### 1.4 How features are enabled

**Three layers, and only three, each with exactly one owner:**

| Layer | Question it answers | Granularity | Who sets it | Precedent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Install** | Is this module's code even in the process? | per deployment | owner, at deploy | superbot-next has *none* — all 49 manifests load unconditionally (R3-D7) |
| **Enable** | Is this feature available in this server? | per guild (+ scope chain) | server owner, in setup | survives in next, guild-scope only (R3-S9, corrected) |
| **Configure** | How does it behave here? | per guild, per setting | staff, in the settings hub | 127 declared settings, real mutation ops exist (**[mine]**: `SET_SCALAR`/`CLEAR_SCALAR`/`BIND`/`UNBIND` in `sb/domain/settings/ops.py`) |

The regression to fix is the **Install** layer. superbot-next removed deploy-time selection entirely and did *not* replace it — and simultaneously made boot fault-intolerant: any single plugin problem aborts the whole boot (R3-D6), where superbot isolates each of 59 extensions in its own try/except and demotes the affected subsystem to INTERNAL rather than crashing (R3-S1, R4-S02). **The successor takes superbot's fault isolation and superbot-next's auto-discovery, and adds back an explicit enabled-modules list.** That is not a compromise; it is three independent properties that were never in conflict.

A fourth pseudo-layer must be *deleted*, not designed: today `governance` can hide a subsystem per guild, but the help category map is a module-level constant, so BTD6 remains a permanent top-level category in every server whether or not the subsystem is enabled (D-D11). **Enablement must reach the presentation layer, or it is a lie told to the server owner.**

### 1.5 How optional game/community modules fit

The owner's requirement, verbatim (2026-08-23): *"I should be able to add exiting cogs to it on demand, or be able to slightly alter an existing cog so that it works with this bot."*

**Neither bot satisfies this, and the fleet's adversarial pass is what proved it.** superbot-next has the only out-of-tree plugin contract in the estate — declared facets, hash pins, a real load path (B-S11, M8-S07) — but: (a) the fence reserves `stores`, `data_invariants` and `wizard_sections` as host-owned, and **29 of its own 49 subsystems declare `stores`**, so 59% of the bot could not ship as a plugin under its own contract (R3-D5); (b) the one gate behind the requirement returns an empty problem list, commented *"nothing to prove"*, when the exemplars are absent — `mv examples /tmp` yields EXIT=0 (F-D08, M8-D04); and (c) **the exemplars are not discord.py cogs at all** — `grep -rn 'commands.Cog|add_cog|setup(bot' examples/` returns zero; they are superbot-next's own manifest grammar (M11-S03, REFUTED). superbot's side is no better: the marginal cost of one cog is 15 modules / 3,389 LOC, but the *shared floor* every cog needs is 148 modules / 30,925 LOC spanning seven top-level packages (A-D03).

**The successor's answer:**

- **A module is a directory with one manifest file, its own tables, and no host edits.** The auto-discovery half of superbot-next is right and cheap (`load_live_manifests` pkgutil-walks `sb/manifest/`, 49 of 49 discovered, R3-S6 corrected) — keep it. The facet fence is wrong: **a module owns its own stores**, declared in its manifest, with the kernel owning only migration ordering and the erasure walk.
- **"Slightly alter an existing cog" is the acceptance test, and it must be executable.** Not two in-tree exemplars in the host's native grammar. The gate is: *take one real discord.py cog from `/home/user/superbot/disbot/cogs/`, apply a documented adapter shim, and boot it in the successor* — with the checker **failing when the corpus is empty**, which is the exact vacuity F-D08 found.
- **Content is not a module.** BTD6's 74 commands and Project Moon's Limbus knowledge are *data with a thin renderer*, not architecture. They ship as content packs a module reads, so the largest single mass in the estate stops being a code-review burden.

### 1.6 What the AI is for, and what it may and may not do

**superbot's AI design is the genuine article and superbot-next did not improve it — it shrank it.** superbot carries 36 tools; 35 return data and the 36th, `open_support_ticket`, validates eligibility and *emits an event so a human clicks a button* — the model cannot write a row (M4-S3). Authority is derived from verified Discord state, never message text, and checked twice (M4-S4). Untrusted text is wrapped with forged delimiters disarmed (M4-S11). Redaction is applied at the provider boundary and to every tool result re-entering context (M4-S7). And the strongest integration is the one where the model is a *paragraph-writer bolted to a deterministic answer*: `btd6_ai_service._augment_with_ai` returns the deterministic response unchanged on degraded gateway, invalid JSON, missing key, empty explanation or exception, and only ever writes `follow_up` (M4-S6).

superbot-next inherited the machinery (24 of 30 kernel AI files name a disbot source in their own first 12 lines, M4-D12) and registers **8 tools, all BTD6 lookups** (**[mine]**, `sb/domain/ai/tools.py`) — zero side-effect-capable tools exist anywhere in the tree (M10-D3).

**The successor's AI contract, stated as product rules:**

| The AI **may** | The AI **may not** |
|---|---|
| Read, summarise, and explain — over tools whose authority is derived from the caller's live Discord permissions | Write anything. Not one row, not one role, not one message deletion |
| Add prose to a deterministic answer, where removing the prose leaves a correct answer | Be the *only* path to any capability |
| Propose an action and emit an event that renders a button a human presses | Decide whether an action is allowed |
| Refuse, and say why | Invent a number. Grounding is token-matched, not substring-matched (M4-D9 measured the substring bug: "Round 1234" whitelists "123") |
| Fail closed, silently, to the deterministic path | Take a message's word for who the speaker is |

**What must work without AI: everything.** Not "most things." Four feature flags already layer strictly with the safe default at each level, and the default provider is deterministic so a fresh deploy makes no external call (M4-S9, corrected). Every command, every panel, every moderation action, every game, and the entire setup journey must be reachable and complete with `AI_ENABLED=false`. The AI is a **surface**, never a **dependency** — spider-bot demonstrates the discipline at small scale, constructing a client only when both the flag and a key are present (M12-S04, corrected).

**One structural change from both bots:** in both, the conversational AI is a stage on the `on_message` pipeline, so it dies with the message_content intent alongside the prefix commands (C-D12, M4-S5 corrected). In the successor the AI is **an invocable capability first** (`/ask`, a context menu on a message, a thread) and a passive listener second, so the one capability most likely to be worth paying for is not hostage to the intent most likely to be denied.

### 1.7 What makes it feel coherent rather than 50 unrelated cogs

Coherence is not a folder layout. Four mechanisms, in the order a user meets them:

1. **One front door with stated purposes.** spider-bot has the cleanest instance in the estate and it is 8 lines of data per entry: a module-level `ROUTES` tuple where every route carries a `label`, an `emoji`, an **audience**, and a `purpose` written in plain language for a human — *"An idea, or how something feels to play"*, *"Something broken, with the details that make it fixable"* (**[mine]**, `spiderbot/ui/routes.py`). The audience is re-resolved from live Discord state on every render and every press, so opening a panel is never taken as authorisation for what happens next. Scale that shape: one home surface, categories filtered by what the viewer may actually use, each carrying a sentence about *why you would press it*.

2. **A closed presentation vocabulary the kernel owns.** Both good instances exist: superbot-next's error copy is one 28-line table in the kernel rather than per-handler strings (D-S03, corrected: 3 call sites); spider-bot locks its emoji set and semantic colours with tests that walk the real filesystem and the real shipped embed objects (M12-S08, corrected — real population, non-blocking CI). The successor centralises **colour, emoji, embed skeleton, denial copy, empty-state copy, and confirmation copy** in the kernel, so 50 modules cannot produce 50 dialects.

3. **Navigation the author cannot forget.** superbot-next's renderer injects Help/Home/Back/page-turn in one block rather than per panel (M9-S01) — the right idea, reaching only 96 of 314 panels because 218 declare `renderer_override` (E-D2, M9-D01). superbot's version reaches ~59 of 280 View classes in practice (E-S1, REFUTED at its stated 217). **The successor makes injected navigation the only path and deletes the override**, which is affordable precisely because there will be far fewer panels.

4. **One journey through settings.** Every module's configuration renders in one hub from a declaration, with no per-module UI code. superbot's `SubsystemSchema` does this for 19 cogs (R3-S3) and superbot-next's settings grammar does it for 127 settings across the corpus (**[mine]**). Both work. The failure in both is *registry blindness*: starboard is a live, permission-gated, three-table production cog that appears in superbot's `SUBSYSTEMS` registry **not at all**, so it is invisible to Help, to the settings browser, and to governance — while the reachability checker reports "19 reachable · 0 GAP", EXIT=0, because it certifies from a source literal rather than the live catalogue (M2-D1, M1-D04, R3-D1).

### 1.8 How new features join the journey

The strongest thing in either repo on this axis is superbot's `scripts/new_subsystem.py check`: an **executable** integration standard naming 14 touch-points, which correctly found 6 missing for starboard on first invocation this session (R3-S10 corrected, R3-D11). Its defect is that nothing ever runs it over the whole cog set — it takes one key by hand and appears in no workflow. superbot-next's answer is the opposite trade: registration collapses to one auto-discovered file, repaid by three regenerated committed artifacts and a boot gate that refuses to start on divergence (R3-S6 corrected, R3-D12, M8-S02).

**The successor takes both halves and closes the loop:**

- A new module is **one directory + one manifest file**. No registry edit, no extension list.
- The integration standard is a **sweep, not a spot-check**: a checker that walks every installed module and asserts each has a help entry, a settings entry if it declares settings, a category, an authority declaration, and — the one nobody has — **at least one reachable user-facing outcome**. That last assertion is what 153 zero-action panels and starboard-invisible-to-help have in common (R6-D06: *both* repos' reachability guards assert registration and never usefulness).
- **The guard must fail on an empty population.** This is the fleet's single most reusable finding: 19 of 77 executable guards are vacuous-capable, 5 are structurally empty (R2, M11-D09), and the one guard in either repo that makes an empty population a *test failure* is superbot's help-reachability negative control, which `pytest.fail()`s when its target is not present (F-S02 — noting the correction that its *input* is still a model of the click tree, not the rendered components).

## Part 3 — The Non-Goals

Each line is something that deliberately does not exist in the successor, with the one reason.

1. **Byte-parity with either existing bot as an acceptance criterion.** The oracle is a build the owner has said is not the desired product (C-D11), and choosing it *caused* fabricated diagnostics, a frozen 58-entry cog roster, and 128 jargon strings that can no longer be improved without reddening a required check (M11-D05, D-D07).
2. **A frozen legacy command vocabulary as a required check.** `compat-frozen.json` makes 413 prefix names and 135 aliases the one contract a merge cannot break, while the modern-surface gates are non-required (C-D04, E-D11) — it protects exactly the wrong thing.
3. **Prefix commands as the primary invocation surface.** 386 of 413 commands today die with a privileged intent Discord can withdraw (C-D01). Prefix survives as a thin alias layer; it is not the product.
4. **A bot that can be silent.** Every invocation produces exactly one outcome, always visible (D-D01, D-S01).
5. **Any surface that renders the bot's own state as a literal.** 12 files do this today, including a database-health card that reports 103/103 against 57 migrations (R1-D3, R1-D8).
6. **Settings, toggles or buttons whose consumers are not armed.** 23 safety settings render over unarmed engines; a greeting is ON and cannot fire; a Cog Manager ships live pagination over dead buttons (**[mine]**, D-D04, R3-D8).
7. **Panels with no actions.** 153 of 314 (49%, settled) — a panel with nothing to press is a message, and should be sent as one.
8. **Escape hatches from the panel grammar.** 218 of 314 panels declare `renderer_override`, and the ratchet that was supposed to prevent this counts a different marker whose population is zero (E-D2, M9-D01, F-D06). One rendering path or none.
9. **Guards whose population may be empty.** Five gates in superbot-next are structurally empty and pass; nine are emptiable or model-based (M11-D09). **An empty population is a test failure, not a pass.**
10. **Absence-only acceptance.** All six checks in the required `architecture` context assert that something is *not* present; a bot that does nothing passes all of them perfectly (F-D10). At least one gate must assert a floor on what works.
11. **A development gallery as a product surface.** UX Lab (H1).
12. **The Claude-Code dispatch bridge.** Already ruled out by the owner on 2026-07-05 and still shipping (H2).
13. **Multi-tenant scale apparatus** — sharding, per-guild quotas, a web dashboard, an onboarding funnel. *(Conditional on the OWNER_DECISION in §1.1; recommended default is to omit.)*
14. **Content as architecture.** BTD6 and Project Moon become versioned data packs behind a thin module, not 36,410 lines inside the runtime (G1, G2).
15. **A second bot.** spider-bot is a separate live product with its own audience; the successor absorbs its *patterns* (the route registry with plain-language purposes, the audience re-resolution, no-premature-persistence) and not its scope.

## Part 5 — The three things that decide whether this rebuild is different

1. **Change the oracle.** Acceptance is "a member can do X and the effect is Y", asserted over rendered components and read-back rows — not "the bytes match the bot we are replacing." The corpus proves it needs replacing: 485 of 533 goldens are one command in, 23 of 863 component bindings are ever clicked (2.7%), 38 goldens assert literally nothing, and 36 pin a refusal or usage error as the expected behaviour (M11-D04, F-D01, R5-D02, R5-D04).

2. **Make one gate assert a floor.** Every required check in both repos asserts absence or self-consistency. A bot with all 863 controls wired to resolvable no-op handlers, one golden per subsystem and a forged sign-off row passes 7/7 green (F, F-D04: I confirmed a fully forged verification record validates with zero problems). One gate must say: *N capabilities produce a real, asserted, user-visible effect* — and must red when N is zero.

3. **Make the owner's own requirement executable.** "Add an existing cog on demand" is currently proven by two exemplars written in the host's own grammar, behind a checker that returns "nothing to prove" when they are absent (M11-S03 REFUTED, F-D08). The successor's acceptance test is: **take one real cog out of `/home/user/superbot/disbot/cogs/`, apply the documented shim, boot it, and click something in it** — with the gate failing when the corpus is empty. That single test would have caught more of this fleet's findings than any other mechanism in either repo.

**Lane:** synthesis. **Pins:** superbot @5e3a667b · superbot-next @d5f66dc2 · spider-bot @bf4d7527.
**Method:** designed against the fleet's 137 standing rows + 62 refutations, plus 8 measurements I took myself (marked `[SYNTH-n]`, all reproducible from the read-only clones). I did not boot either bot; no lane in this fleet did.

## 0. What the evidence forces before any design starts

Five constraints are not negotiable because they are measured, not argued.

**C1 — The invocation surface is the biggest single decision, and both bots got it wrong.**
386 of 413 of superbot-next's compiled commands are prefix-only; 27 (6.5%) survive a `message_content` denial (`C-D01`). superbot is 243 prefix commands against 30 app_commands, zero hybrids (`D-D08`). The two gates that would guard a modern surface govern 18 of 413 (`C-D03`) and 4 of 413 (`C-S04`, REFUTED as self-satisfying). And the successor's *required* CI check freezes the 2020-era prefix vocabulary — 413 names + 135 aliases — while leaving the slash surface ungated (`C-D04`). superbot's own analysis named the escape on 2026-07-03, five days before superbot-next's first commit, and shipped it once for `/btd6` (`C-D02`, `C-S05`). It was not generalised.

**C2 — The acceptance oracle shapes the implementation. Byte-parity to a rejected bot produced fabricated production behaviour.**
Twelve files freeze the old bot's runtime state and ship it as live output — a `!check_database` card that reports "103/103 migrations" over a tree with 57 migration files (`R1-D3`), a Server Management health badge that is a constant (`R1-D6`), a `!coglist` of 58 old-bot cog module names committed *because a golden pinned those bytes* while the correct live implementation sits unused two files away (`R1-D7`, `M11-D05`). The class was found by the repo's own review on 2026-07-12, flagged `⚑ live-misleading`, and parked (`R1-D11`). This is the single most expensive lesson in the corpus: **the oracle you choose becomes the code you ship.**

**C3 — The dominant defect class is the vacuous guard, and its root cause is process-global registries.**
19 of 77 executable guards are vacuity-capable (`R2`); 5 required gates are structurally empty (`M11-D09`); the flagship navigation golden is empty twice over (`R2-D01`). `[SYNTH-1]` measured the root: superbot-next carries **112 `*_for_tests` reset functions across 106 files** (`grep -rnE "def [a-z_]+_for_tests\(" sb/`), 92 of them `clear_*`/`reset_*`, each guarding a module-level mutable dict. superbot carries 42, of which **36 share one discoverable hook name `_reset_for_tests`** that an executable guard rglobs and sweeps (`C-S02`). *Both prior rows are wrong*: `E-D6` said 92 vs 1; `C-S02`'s correction said 6. The real finding is not the count — it is that superbot made global-state reset **discoverable**, and superbot-next made it **enumerable by hand**, which is exactly how an autouse fixture came to empty a guard's population without anyone noticing.

**C4 — Cog portability is an owner requirement that neither bot satisfies, and the numbers are known.**
superbot: marginal cost 15 modules / 3,389 LOC per cog, on a **shared floor of 148 modules / 30,925 LOC spanning seven top-level packages** (`A-S08`, `A-D03`). superbot-next: floor 12 modules / 2,050 LOC — but marginal cost 52 modules / **10,149 LOC** per subsystem (`A-D08`), and its plugin contract fences `stores` out, so **29 of its own 49 subsystems could not ship as plugins** (`R3-D5`). One repo has the right floor, the other the right increment; neither has both.

**C5 — The abstractions that failed are the ones with one consumer, and the estate already measured it.**
Panel grammar: 218 of 314 panels (69%) bypass it, and 60 of the 96 that use it belong to a single subsystem — `help` (`E-D2`, `E-D3`). Workflow/saga engine: 173 of 185 legs are single DB legs, 0 irreversible, compensators never fire (`B-D11`); idempotency 0 of 175 `DURABLE_ONCE` (`B-D03`); confirmation 0 of 175 (`B-D05`). Outbox: 763 LOC serving 1 event of 25 (`M9-D06`). Manifest vocabulary: 107 of 237 declared field names never given a non-default value (`M9-D08`). **The rebuild's kernel is 20,486 LOC (`R6-D09`) and most of it is unexercised.**

Everything below follows from C1–C5.
